1.question: When was Republic Act No. 10863 (Customs Modernization and Tariff Act) signed into law?
1.reason: RA 10863 (CMTA) was signed into law on 30 May 2016 (Primer p.1).

2.question: Which laws were repealed by the CMTA?

choices.C: PD 1464 (Tariff and Customs Code of 1978, as amended) and PD 1853 of 1982

2.reason: The CMTA repealed PD 1464 (TCCP of 1978, as amended) and PD 1853 of 1982 (Primer p.1).

3.question: PD No. 1853 of 1982, which was repealed by the CMTA, required what?

choices.A: Deposits of duties at the time of opening of letter of credit covering imports
choices.B: Payment of duties only after release of the goods

3.reason: PD 1853 required deposits of duties at the time of opening of letter of credit covering imports and for other purposes (Primer p.1).

4.question: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the CMTA?

choices.A: To adopt clear and transparent customs rules consistent with international standards
choices.B: To employ modern practices and utilize information and communications technology
choices.C: To institute professionalism and meritocracy in customs tax administration
choices.D: To ban the importation of all competing agricultural products

4.reason: The listed CMTA objectives include harmonized procedures, transparency, consultation, fair appellate remedies, modern practices and meritocracy. Banning all competing agricultural imports is not one of them (Primer p.1).

5.question: Which of the following goods is PROHIBITED (not merely restricted) for importation and exportation under the CMTA?

choices.B: Infringing goods as defined under the Intellectual Property Code and related laws

5.reason: Infringing goods are in the prohibited list. Firearms, lottery tickets and opium pipes are in the list of goods prohibited 'except when authorized by law or regulation' (Primer pp.2-3).

6.question: Which of the following may be imported only by the government or a person duly authorized by the Dangerous Drugs Board for medicinal purposes?

choices.A: Marijuana, opium, poppies, coca leaves, heroin or other narcotics or synthetic drugs

6.reason: The exception for the government or persons authorized by the Dangerous Drugs Board for medicinal purposes applies to narcotics and synthetic drugs (Primer p.3).

7.question: The restriction on the importation or exportation of the restricted goods under the CMTA shall also include the restriction on their:
7.reason: The restriction to import or export the goods shall include the restriction on their transit (Primer p.3).

8.question: The Tariff Commission may deputize or delegate its function of rendering rulings on tariff classification disputes to an appropriate government agency, but such delegation shall NOT extend beyond how many years from the effectivity of the CMTA?
8.reason: The delegation shall not extend beyond three (3) years from the effectivity of the Act (Primer p.4).

9.question: Under Section 1100, within how many days from receipt of a properly documented application must the Tariff Commission render a ruling on advance ruling for tariff classification?
9.reason: The Commission shall render a ruling within thirty (30) days from receipt of a properly documented application (Primer p.4).

10.question: Rulings of the Tariff Commission on commodity classification are binding upon the Bureau of Customs unless:

choices.A: the Secretary of Finance shall rule otherwise
choices.C: the Commissioner of Customs shall rule otherwise
choices.D: the NEDA Board shall rule otherwise

10.reason: Section 1100: the Commission's rulings on commodity classification are binding upon the Bureau unless the Secretary of Finance shall rule otherwise (Primer p.4).

11.question: Under Section 1102, who acts on an application for advance ruling on origin, and within what period from receipt of the application and supporting documents?
11.reason: The application for advance ruling on origin is filed with the Commissioner, who shall act on it within thirty (30) days (Primer p.4).

12.question: Under the Flexible Clause (Section 1608), the increased rate of import duty shall in no case be higher than a maximum of:
12.reason: Section 1608(a)(1): in no case shall the increased rate be higher than one hundred percent (100%) ad valorem (Primer p.5).

13.question: Under Section 1608(a)(3), the President may impose an additional duty on all imports not exceeding:
13.reason: The additional duty on all imports shall not exceed ten percent (10%) ad valorem (Primer p.5).

14.question: Under the Flexible Clause (Section 1608), the President exercises the power to modify import duties upon the recommendation of the:
14.reason: Section 1608(a): the President, upon the recommendation of the NEDA, is empowered to increase, reduce or remove duties (Primer p.5).

15.question: After the termination of public hearings, within how many days shall the Tariff Commission submit its findings and recommendations to the NEDA under Section 1608(b)?
15.reason: The Commission shall submit its findings and recommendations to the NEDA within thirty (30) days after the termination of the public hearings (Primer p.5).

16.question: When does an order issued by the President under Section 1608 take effect?

choices.C: Thirty (30) days after promulgation, except an additional duty not exceeding 10% which takes effect at the President's discretion

16.reason: Section 1608(d): orders take effect thirty (30) days after promulgation, except the additional duty not exceeding 10% ad valorem, which takes effect at the discretion of the President (Primer p.5).

17.question: The power delegated to the President under Section 1608 may be exercised only when:

choices.D: a state of emergency is declared

17.reason: Section 1608(e): the delegated power shall be exercised only when Congress is not in session (Primer p.5).

18.question: The power delegated to the President under Section 1608 may be withdrawn or terminated by Congress through a:
18.reason: Section 1608(f): the power may be withdrawn or terminated by Congress through a joint resolution (Primer p.5).

19.question: Under Section 1608(c), in modifying the form of duty, the ad valorem or specific equivalents shall be based on imports from:

choices.C: the principal competing foreign country for the most recent representative period

19.reason: The corresponding ad valorem or specific equivalents of the duty with respect to imports from the principal competing foreign country for the most recent representative period shall be used as basis (Primer p.5).

20.question: Before a trade agreement is concluded, the Tariff Commission shall seek information and advice from which agencies under Section 1609(d)?

choices.D: DTI, DA, DOF, DENR, DFA and BSP

20.reason: Section 1609(d) names the DTI, DA, DOF, DENR, DFA and BSP, and other sources the Commission deems appropriate (Primer p.6).

21.question: Under Section 1609(b), the President may suspend the application of a concession to goods of a specific country because of acts or policies which tend to defeat the purposes of the section, including the operations of:
21.reason: Section 1609(b) mentions acts or policies, including the operations of international cartels (Primer p.6).

22.question: Under Section 1609(e), who evaluates the Commission's report on a trade agreement and submits recommendations to the President?
22.reason: Section 1609(e)(2): the NEDA shall evaluate the report of the Commission and submit recommendations to the President (Primer p.6).

23.question: Section 1609(c) states that nothing in the section shall be construed to give authority to:

choices.D: cancel or reduce the indebtedness of any foreign country to the Philippines

23.reason: Nothing shall be construed to give authority to cancel or reduce the indebtedness of any foreign country to the Philippines or any claim of the Philippines against any foreign country (Primer p.6).

24.question: How many Tariff Reform Programs (TRPs) were undertaken starting from 1980?
24.reason: Four (4) TRPs were undertaken from 1980 (Primer p.8).

25.question: TRP-I was undertaken during which period?
25.reason: TRP-I proceeded as scheduled from 1981 to 1985 and covered Chapters 1 to 97 of Section 104 of the TCCP (Primer p.8).

26.question: TRP-I narrowed the tariff band from 10%-100% to 10%-50%. The average nominal tariff fell from 42% in 1981 to what level at the end of TRP-I?
26.reason: The average nominal tariff fell from 42% in 1981 to 28% at the end of TRP-I (Primer p.9).

27.question: EO 470, signed on 20 July 1991 and effective 24 August 1991 under TRP-II, covered about what share of total tariff lines?
27.reason: EO 470 covered about 80% of the total number of tariff lines, with a five-year phase-in from 1991 to 1995 (Primer p.9).

28.question: After TRP-II in July 1995, almost 95% of total tariff lines were dutiable at:
28.reason: Almost 95% of lines were dutiable at 3%, 10%, 20% and 30%; the rest were at 0%, 5%, 15%, 25% and 50% (Primer p.9).

29.question: Under TRP-II, the number of HS tariff lines was reduced from 6,193 to 5,561 due to:

choices.A: simplification of the tariff nomenclature, where lines that would have the same rates were combined into one
choices.B: removal of agricultural products from coverage
choices.C: creation of new tariff lines for IT products

29.reason: The 10% reduction was due to simplification of the tariff nomenclature, combining lines that would eventually have the same duty rate, for ease of customs administration (Primer p.9).

30.question: The issuance of which EO on 18 July 1994 marked the onset of TRP-III?
30.reason: The issuance of EO 189 on 18 July 1994 marked the onset of TRP-III (Primer p.10).

31.question: Under EO 264, the final rate structure under TRP-III will consist of a uniform tariff rate of:
31.reason: The final structure is a uniform 5% in 2004, after a penultimate stage of 3% (raw materials and intermediate goods) and 10% (finished products) in 2003 (Primer p.10).

32.question: EO 313 (effective 07 May 1996) provided interim tariff protection to sensitive agricultural products and identified a total of how many tariff lines subject to tariff quotas?
32.reason: EO 313 identified a total of 170 tariff lines subject to tariff quotas as part of the Philippines' WTO commitment (Primer p.10).

33.question: The more flexible tariff structure adopted under TRP-IV consisted of which rates?
33.reason: TRP-IV used 3%, 5%, 7%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25% and 30% in place of the earlier 3%, 10%, 20% and 30% (Primer p.11).

34.question: How many industries identified as 'Philippine Winners' were initially targeted for re-calibration of tariff rates under TRP-IV?
34.reason: Twenty-two (22) industries identified as 'Philippine Winners' were initially targeted (Primer p.11).

35.question: EO 486 (effective 10 July 1998) reduced the number of tariff lines subject to tariff quotas from 170 under EO 313 to:
35.reason: EO 486 reduced the tariff lines subject to quotas from 170 to 144 (Primer p.11).

36.question: The 2015 comprehensive review of the MFN tariff structure (for 2016 to 2020) was concluded upon the issuance of which EO?
36.reason: The review was concluded with EO 20 signed on 27 April 2017 (Primer p.12).

37.question: Under EO 61 (signed 17 October 2011, effective 14 January 2012), tariff rates were maintained at 2010 levels for what percentage of tariff lines?
37.reason: Tariff rates under EO 61 were maintained at 2010 levels for 96% of tariff lines (Primer p.12).

38.question: EO 20, s. 2017 maintained the tariff rates for 85% of total tariff lines. How many lines is this?
38.reason: EO 20 maintained rates for 85% of total tariff lines (8,460 lines) and reduced rates for 722 lines (Primer p.13).

39.question: The adoption of AHTN 2017 on 28 July 2017 increased the number of Philippine tariff lines by 11%, from 10,004 to:
39.reason: The tariff lines increased from 10,004 (AHTN 2012) to 11,058 (AHTN 2017) (Primer p.15).

40.question: As of June 2020, which product has the highest MFN tariff rate, and at what rate?
40.reason: Rice and sugar have the highest MFN rates at 50% and 65%, respectively (Primer p.15).

41.question: EO 82 (took effect 17 June 2019) modified the rates of duty on:

choices.B: mechanically deboned meat of chicken and turkey, and turkey meat and its offals

41.reason: EO 82 covered mechanically deboned meat of chicken, and turkey, and turkey meat and its offals (Primer pp.14, 20).

42.question: EO 113 (took effect 6 May 2020) temporarily modified the MFN rates of import duty on:

choices.A: crude petroleum oil and refined petroleum products

42.reason: EO 113 covers crude petroleum oil and refined petroleum products under Section 1611 of the CMTA (Primer pp.14, 20).

43.question: EO 23 (took effect 24 May 2017) was issued in relation to:

choices.C: 36 non-rice tariff lines, in relation to the special treatment for rice under the WTO

43.reason: EO 23 covered 36 non-rice tariff lines in relation to the special treatment of rice under the WTO (Primer p.14).

44.question: In the last fifteen (15) years, the overall average MFN tariffs stayed within the range of:
44.reason: Overall average tariffs stayed within 7% to 8% over the last 15 years (Table 1.1, Primer p.14).

45.question: The Effective Protection Rate (EPR) is the percentage excess of domestic value added, made possible by tariffs and other protective measures on the product and its inputs, over:
45.reason: Annex A defines EPR as the percentage excess of domestic value added over world market value added (Primer p.21).

46.question: In the EPR formula, what does Pbj represent?

choices.B: Selling price of the product, net of sales tax
choices.C: Cost of imported raw materials used
choices.D: Actual tariff rate on material input i

46.reason: Pbj is the border price of the product, while Psj is the selling price net of sales tax (Annex A, Primer p.21).

47.question: In the EPR formula, Aij(m) represents:

choices.A: cost of local raw materials used
choices.C: cost of imported raw materials used
choices.D: selling price net of sales tax

47.reason: Aij(m) is the cost of imported raw materials used. Aij(l) is the cost of local raw materials (Annex A, Primer p.21).

48.question: EO 890 (10 June 2010) eliminated the 3% duty on crude oil, petroleum products and asphalts imported from:
48.reason: EO 890 eliminated the 3% duty on crude oil, petroleum products and asphalts imported from non-ASEAN (Table 1.3, Primer p.19).

49.question: EO 418 (04 April 2005) temporarily imposed an additional specific duty of Php500,000 on:

choices.B: used motor vehicles except trucks, buses and special purpose vehicles

49.reason: EO 418 imposed the additional specific duty on used motor vehicles except trucks, buses and special purpose vehicles. EO 477 later amended it (Table 1.3, Primer p.18).

50.question: Which EO provided a recalibrated tariff structure as a result of the 2005 comprehensive tariff review?
50.reason: EO 574 (signed 04 November 2006) provided the recalibrated structure from the 2005 review, which took effect in 2007 (Table 1.3, Primer pp.12, 18).

51.question: When did RA No. 11203 (The Rice Tariffication Law) take effect?
51.reason: RA 11203 was signed on 14 February 2019 and took effect on 5 March 2019 (Primer p.22).

52.question: RA No. 11203 amends which law?
52.reason: RA 11203 amends RA No. 8178, otherwise known as the Agricultural Tariffication Act (Primer p.22).

53.question: As defined in RA 11203, 'tariffication' refers to:

choices.A: the lifting of all existing quantitative restrictions such as import quotas or prohibitions on agricultural products and replacing them with tariffs
choices.B: the increase of tariffs on all agricultural products to 100%
choices.C: the replacement of tariffs with import quotas
choices.D: the exemption of rice from all duties and taxes

53.reason: Tariffication is the lifting of all existing QRs such as import quotas or prohibitions on agricultural products and replacing these restrictions with tariffs (Primer p.22, footnote 3).

54.question: To give farmers equivalent protection, RA 11203 imposes a tariff rate on rice imports of at least:
54.reason: One objective is to provide farmers equivalent protection with the imposition of 35% or higher tariff rates on rice imports (Primer p.22).

55.question: Under Section 5 of RA 11203, the bound rate on rice imported outside the ASEAN region is 180% or the tariff equivalent calculated by the Tariff Commission (WTO methodology, approved by the NEDA Board), whichever is:

choices.D: set by the Secretary of Finance

55.reason: The bound rate shall be 180% or the tariff equivalent calculated by the Commission and approved by the NEDA Board, whichever is higher (Primer p.22).

56.question: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the Rice Tariffication Law?

choices.A: Lower domestic rice prices to levels affordable to the majority of the population
choices.B: Allow private traders, big or small, to participate in importing rice
choices.C: Give farmers the opportunity to earn in the world market by lifting the restriction on rice exports
choices.D: Increase government intervention in the domestic rice market

56.reason: The law aims for the market to function effectively with reduced or no government intervention, so increasing intervention is not an objective (Primer p.22).

57.question: The IRR of RA 11203 was issued through Joint Memorandum Circular No. 01-2019 of which agencies?

choices.C: DA, DTI and the Tariff Commission

57.reason: JMC No. 01-2019 of the NEDA, DA and DBM was issued on 05 April 2019 (Primer p.23).

58.question: Among the salient provisions of the IRR of RA 11203 are guidelines on:

choices.B: the President's powers and the enforcement of safeguard measures in emergencies like a sudden rise or drop in domestic prices
choices.C: registration of rice importers with the BOI

58.reason: The IRR contains guidelines on the President's powers and safeguard measures in emergency situations such as sudden rise or drop in domestic prices (Primer p.23).

59.question: RA 11203 already took effect on 05 March 2019, before its IRR was issued, because it has:

choices.C: self-executing provisions such as on applicable tariff rates

59.reason: RA 11203 took effect on 05 March 2019 with its self-executing provisions such as on applicable tariff rates (Primer p.23).

60.question: RA No. 8502 is otherwise known as the:
60.reason: RA 8502 is the Jewelry Industry Development Act of 1998, signed on 13 February 1998 (Primer p.24).

61.question: RA 8502 was signed on 13 February 1998. When did it take effect?
61.reason: RA 8502 took effect on 09 July 1998. Its IRR (DOF and BOC) took effect on 25 January 1999 (Primer p.24).

62.question: Under RA 8502, jewelry enterprises get an additional deduction from taxable income equal to what percentage of expenses incurred in approved training schemes?
62.reason: The incentive is an additional deduction of 50% of expenses incurred in training schemes approved by the appropriate agency (Primer p.24).

63.question: Which of the following is an incentive granted under RA 8502?

choices.A: Exemption from income tax for ten years
choices.B: Zero duty on all imported finished jewelry
choices.C: Inclusion of locally manufactured jewelry in the government's tourist duty free shops, including promotion, advertisement and sale
choices.D: Waiver of all BOI registration requirements

63.reason: RA 8502 incentives include zero duty on imported raw materials and capital equipment, excise tax exemption on jewelry, and inclusion of local jewelry in tourist duty free shops (Primer p.24).

64.question: To qualify for incentives under Section 4 of RA 8502, a jewelry enterprise must be duly registered with the:
64.reason: Section 4 of RA 8502 requires jewelry enterprises to be duly registered with the Board of Investments (Primer p.24).

65.question: What was the role of the Tariff Commission in the implementation of RA 8502?

choices.A: Setting the price of gold and silver
choices.D: Providing technical expertise in tariff classification and preparing the list of products and equipment entitled to tax and duty exemption

65.reason: The Commission provided technical expertise in tariff classification and prepared the list of products and equipment entitled to tax and duty exemption (Primer p.25).

66.question: In what year did the Tariff Commission launch the Philippine Tariff Finder (PTF)?
66.reason: The PTF was launched in 2013 as a free online facility. It was upgraded in 2015 to include Rules of Origin and FTA rates (Primer p.26).

67.question: How many Philippine tariff schedules can be accessed on the PTF?
67.reason: All twelve (12) tariff schedules of the Philippines are on the PTF, including MFN, the FTAs and the three PH-EFTA FTA schedules (Primer p.26).

68.question: The PH-EFTA FTA has how many tariff schedules on the PTF?
68.reason: The PH-EFTA FTA has three tariff schedules: NOR, CHE/LIE and ISL (Primer pp.26, 28).

69.question: The PTF is hosted on which website?
69.reason: The PTF is hosted on the Commission's website www.tariffcommission.gov.ph and at finder.tariffcommission.gov.ph (Primer p.26).

70.question: Which PTF menu item links directly to the AHTN 2017 Tariff Book?
70.reason: AHTN 2017 directly links to the AHTN 2017 Tariff Book (Figure 1.4, Primer p.27).

71.question: Which PTF menu item gives an overview of tariff classification using the General Rules for the Interpretation of the HS?
71.reason: The E-Manual on Classification gives an overview of tariff classification using the GIR (Figure 1.4, Primer p.27).

72.question: Which PTF menu item provides overviews of the twelve tariff schedules of the Philippines?
72.reason: Tariff Schedules provides overviews of the twelve (12) tariff schedules of the Philippines (Figure 1.4, Primer p.27).

73.question: What is the first step in using the PTF search, per the Primer?

choices.A: Select the year from the dropdown menu
choices.B: Click the 'Please start your search here' button on the PTF home page
choices.C: Type the AHTN code in the search bar

73.reason: Step a: click the 'Please start your search here' button on the PTF home page, and the search page appears (Primer p.28).

74.question: After a keyword search such as 'corn', the PTF provides an initial listing of subheadings at which levels?
74.reason: The PTF lists all 4-digit, 6-digit and 8-digit subheadings containing the keyword (Primer p.29).

75.question: What does the Tariff Heading Map show?

choices.A: The Rules of Origin of each FTA
choices.C: The parent and sibling codes of the chosen code for reference

75.reason: The Tariff Heading Map results box shows the parent and sibling codes of the chosen code (Primer pp.29-30).

76.question: In the PTF example, popcorn (1005.90.10) is in the Exclusion List (EL) of the AIFTA. What is the applicable tariff?
76.reason: Because popcorn is in the AIFTA Exclusion List, the applicable tariff is the MFN rate of 7% (Figure 1.13, Primer p.32).

77.question: In the PTF example, the ATIGA rate of 0% on postage stamps (4907.00.21) is marked 'Except KH' (Cambodia). What tariff applies to imports from Cambodia?
77.reason: 'Except KH' means the 0% ATIGA rate applies to all ASEAN members except Cambodia, so Cambodia's imports pay the MFN rate of 5% (Figure 1.16, Primer p.33).

78.question: The World Customs Organization (WCO) was established in 1952 as the:
78.reason: The WCO was established in 1952 as the Customs Co-operation Council (CCC) (Primer p.36).

79.question: The WCO has its headquarters in:
79.reason: The WCO has its headquarters in Brussels, Belgium (Primer p.36).

80.question: 'World Customs Organization' is only an informal working name because:

choices.A: the WTO did not approve the name
choices.B: the Convention establishing the CCC has not been amended, so CCC remains its official name
choices.C: the Philippines objected to the name
choices.D: the HS Convention replaced the CCC

80.reason: The WCO adopted the informal working name to indicate its nature, but the Convention establishing the CCC has not been amended (Primer p.36).

81.question: According to the Primer, the WCO has worldwide membership of how many customs administrations, collectively processing about 98% of world trade?
81.reason: The printed text states a worldwide membership of 182 customs administrations (Primer p.36).

82.question: The primary objective of the WCO is to:

choices.A: enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of member customs administrations
choices.B: collect customs duties for its members
choices.D: set the tariff rates of its members

82.reason: The primary objective is to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of member customs administrations (Primer p.36).

83.question: Which of the following is NOT a main function of the WCO?

choices.A: To study all questions relating to cooperation in customs matters
choices.B: To prepare draft Conventions and amendments and recommend their adoption
choices.C: To impose import duties on its member countries
choices.D: To make recommendations, in a conciliatory capacity, for the settlement of disputes on the Conventions

83.reason: The WCO functions are items (a) to (h), such as studying cooperation, preparing draft Conventions, conciliation and cooperating with other organizations. Imposing duties is not one (Primer pp.36-37).

84.question: How are votes allotted among WCO members?

choices.B: Each member has one representative and is entitled to one vote
choices.C: Votes are weighted by share of world trade
choices.D: Only the Council members may vote

84.reason: Delegates discuss customs issues on equal footing. Each member has one representative and is entitled to one vote (Primer p.37).

85.question: The highest body of the WCO, composed of the Directors-General of Customs from all members, is the:
85.reason: The Council is the highest body of the WCO. It meets once a year (Primer p.37).

86.question: The WCO Council is assisted by the Finance Committee and the Policy Commission. How many members does each have?
86.reason: The Council is assisted by the Finance Committee (17 members) and the Policy Commission (24 members) (Primer p.37).

87.question: The Harmonized System (HS) is the amalgamation of which two systems?
87.reason: The HS is the amalgamation of the Customs Co-operation Council Nomenclature (CCCN) and the Standard International Trade Classification (SITC) Revision 2 (Primer p.40).

88.question: The HS is organized into how many Sections and Chapters?
88.reason: The HS is organized into 21 Sections subdivided into 97 Chapters (Primer p.40).

89.question: Which HS Chapter is reserved for future international use?
89.reason: Chapter 77 is reserved for future international use (Primer p.40).

90.question: In the 6-digit HS subheading, the first two digits indicate the:

choices.B: position of the heading in the Chapter

90.reason: The first two digits indicate the Chapter number, the next two the position of the heading in the Chapter, and the last two the subheading number (Primer p.40).

91.question: Sections 1610 and 1611 of the CMTA reflect the HS by providing for, respectively:

choices.A: the HS Convention and the HS Committee
choices.C: the GIR and the list of headings with corresponding rates of import duty
choices.D: advance rulings and rules of origin

91.reason: The HS is reflected in Sections 1610 and 1611 of the CMTA, which provide for the GIR and the list of headings with corresponding import duty rates, respectively (Primer p.42).

92.question: WCO member countries are mandated to adopt the HS up to what digit level?
92.reason: It is mandatory to adopt the HS up to the 6-digit level. Modifications should be done beyond that level (Primer p.40).

93.question: At the tariff-rate line (legal) level a country may assign 8 digits. How many final non-legal digits may be added for statistical reporting, for a total of 10?
93.reason: Two final non-legal digits may be assigned as statistical reporting numbers, for a total of 10 digits (Primer p.40).

94.question: The General Rules for the Interpretation of the HS (GIR) consist of how many rules, and how should they be applied?

choices.A: Six rules, applied in hierarchical order
choices.B: Five rules, applied in any order
choices.D: Four rules, applied by the importer's choice

94.reason: The GIR provide six (6) rules and should be applied in hierarchical order (Primer p.41).

95.question: Section and Chapter Notes, including Subheading Notes, have what legal force in the HS?

choices.C: The same legal force as the GIR

95.reason: Section and Chapter Notes form an integral part of the HS and have the same legal force as the GIR (Primer p.41).

96.question: How often is the Harmonized System Committee convened by the WCO Secretary General to update the HS regularly?
96.reason: The HS Committee is composed of representatives of each contracting party and is convened by the Secretary General twice a year (Primer p.41).

97.question: Which WCO body administers the International Convention on the HS, resolves classification problems and acts as arbitrator in customs disputes between countries?
97.reason: The HS Committee administers the HS Convention and resolves specific classification problems. It also acts as arbitrator in customs disputes between countries (Primer p.38).

98.question: In what year did the ten ASEAN Member States, including the Philippines, adopt the 8-digit ASEAN Harmonized Tariff Nomenclature (AHTN)?
98.reason: The ten AMSs adopted the 8-digit AHTN in 2004, reflecting AMSs' requirements beyond the HS 6-digit level (Primer p.42).

99.question: The Philippine Instrument of Accession to the HS Convention was formally deposited to the WCO on:
99.reason: The Instrument was signed on 23 Sept 1998 and concurred in by the Senate on 5 Feb 2001. It was formally deposited to the WCO on 25 June 2001 (Primer p.42).

100.question: The Philippines formally adopted the HS on July 1, 1988 and implemented it in:
100.reason: The Philippines formally adopted the HS on July 1, 1988 and implemented it in October 1988 (Primer p.42).

101.question: Before its Instrument of Accession was approved, why did the Philippines adopt the HS on a de facto basis?

choices.A: To avoid paying WCO membership fees
choices.B: Because the Senate had not yet been constituted
choices.C: To keep abreast of the latest internationally-accepted nomenclature in goods classification in conducting trade with the rest of the world

101.reason: The Philippines opted to adopt the HS on a de facto basis for the conduct of trade with the rest of the world to keep abreast of the latest internationally-accepted nomenclature (Primer p.42).

102.question: Under HS heading 17.04 (Table 2.1), AMSs further subdivided subheading 1704.90 to provide separate lines for:

choices.A: medicated pastilles and drops, white chocolate, and soft candies containing gelatin
choices.B: chewing gum, cocoa butter and candy floss
choices.C: fresh fruits, nuts and dried fruits
choices.D: medicated syrups, milk chocolate and hard candies

102.reason: AMSs subdivided 1704.90 into medicated pastilles and drops, white chocolate, and soft candies containing gelatin. These 8-digit lines pertain to AHTN lines agreed by AMSs (Primer pp.42-43).

103.question: At its first session, the HS Committee set up which body to revise the HS and prepare amendments to the HS Nomenclature?
103.reason: The HS Committee set up the Harmonized System Review Sub-Committee, tasked with revising the HS and preparing amendments to the HS Nomenclature (Primer p.43).

104.question: Under Article 16 of the HS Convention, the HS Committee agreed to allow an interval of how many years between each recommendation amending the HS Nomenclature?
104.reason: The Committee agreed to an interval of four (4) to six (6) years between each recommendation amending the HS Nomenclature under Article 16 (Primer p.43).

105.question: Following NEDA Board approval on June 27, 2017 and pursuant to EO 688 (s. 1981), the Philippines implemented the 2017 version of the HS starting:
105.reason: The Philippines implemented the HS 2017 amendments starting July 28, 2017 (Primer p.44).

106.question: How many sets of amendments are contained in the HS 2017?
106.reason: There are 233 sets of amendments in the HS 2017 (Primer p.43).

107.question: The HS 2017 amendments on advances in technology created lines for which of the following?

choices.C: Chemicals controlled under the Chemical Weapons Convention
choices.D: Light-emitting diode (LED) lamps, multi-component integrated circuits, and hybrid, plug-in hybrid and all-electric vehicles

107.reason: The technology-related amendments created lines for LED lamps, MCOs, and hybrid, plug-in hybrid and all-electric vehicles. The others fall under environmental and social issues (Primer pp.43-44).

108.question: The Explanatory Notes to the HS consist of how many volumes in English and French?
108.reason: The Explanatory Notes consist of five (5) volumes. They do not form an integral part of the HS Convention but are the official interpretation of the HS at international level (Primer p.44).

109.question: The AHTN is an 8-digit commodity nomenclature based on the HS of the WCO. Who conceptualized it?
109.reason: The AHTN was conceptualized by the ten ASEAN Member States to have a common tariff nomenclature. The first AHTN Code, using the HS 2002 edition, was adopted in 2004 (Primer p.46).

110.question: In the AHTN code, the 7th and 8th digits are assigned to:
110.reason: Adhering to the HS 6-digit level, the 7th and 8th digits of the AHTN Code are assigned to ASEAN subheadings (Primer p.46).

111.question: The AHTN serves as the base for preferential tariff purposes in:

choices.D: the ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) and other free trade areas

111.reason: The AHTN is used as a uniform tariff nomenclature within ASEAN, a base for preferential tariff purposes in AFTA and other FTAs, and a base for collecting trade statistics (Primer p.46).

112.question: The AHTN Protocol, which defines the legal framework for the implementation of the AHTN, was signed by the ten ASEAN governments in Manila on:
112.reason: The AHTN Protocol was signed on 07 August 2003 in Manila (Primer p.47).

113.question: The Second Protocol to amend the Protocol Governing the Implementation of the AHTN was signed on 08 April 2010 in:
113.reason: The Second Protocol was signed on 08 April 2010 in Viet Nam (Primer p.47).

114.question: Which ASEAN body is responsible for monitoring, reviewing and supervising all aspects of the implementation of the AHTN Protocol?
114.reason: The ASEAN Directors-General of Customs monitor, review and supervise all aspects of AHTN Protocol implementation (Primer p.47).

115.question: Which ASEAN body is the forum for all decisions relating to the implementation of the AHTN Protocol?
115.reason: The ASEAN Finance Ministers Meeting is the forum for all decisions relating to AHTN Protocol implementation. The ASEAN Secretariat provides support (Primer p.47).

116.question: Under the AHTN Protocol, each AMS shall apply the AHTN up to which level for all trade transactions for tariff, statistical and other purposes?
116.reason: Each AMS shall abide by the HS Code and apply the AHTN up to the 8-digit level (Primer p.47).

117.question: The Philippines uses alpha-numeric codes beyond the 8-digit AHTN level. Which tariff line in Table 2.3 carries such a code and a 5% rate for 2018-2020?

choices.D: 8417.10.00 - Furnaces for roasting, melting or heat-treatment of ores

117.reason: 8417.80.00A (waste incinerators) has a 5% rate. 8417.80.00B (other) is 7%, bakery ovens 7%, parts 1% and 8417.10.00 is 0% (Primer pp.47-48).

118.question: One criterion for providing a subheading in the AHTN is that import and/or export of the product amount to at least what value for the last three (3) years preceding the review?
118.reason: Among the criteria, imports and/or exports must amount to at least US$1 million for the last three years preceding the review (Primer p.48).

119.question: In what instances may the AHTN be amended?

choices.A: Only upon order of the WTO
choices.B: Only when the Tariff Commission decides
choices.D: When there are amendments to the HS Nomenclature or amendments to the ASEAN Codes for simplification, AMS requirements, or changes in technology and trade

119.reason: The AHTN may be amended when there are (i) amendments to the HS Nomenclature and (ii) amendments to the ASEAN Codes for simplification, AMS requirements and changes in technology and trade (Primer p.48).

120.question: Decisions of the ASEAN Directors-General of Customs on proposed AHTN amendments are made by:
120.reason: The Directors-General of Customs are the forum to allow amendments and may convene an experts' panel. Their decisions are made by consensus (Primer p.48).

121.question: The Tariff Commission is mandated by which EO, dated 01 May 1981, to align the Philippine Tariff Nomenclature with all future amendments to the CCCN?
121.reason: The Commission is mandated by EO 688, dated 01 May 1981, to align the Philippine Tariff Nomenclature with all future amendments to the CCCN (Primer p.49).

122.question: The Philippines is bound to implement the AHTN by Article 4 of the ASEAN Agreement on Customs, dated:
122.reason: The Philippines is bound by Article 4 of the ASEAN Agreement on Customs dated 01 March 1997 and by the AHTN Protocol (Primer p.49).

123.question: After the Commission submits its report on AHTN amendments to the NEDA, which committee considers it?

choices.D: Committee on Tariff and Related Matters (CTRM)

123.reason: The report is submitted to NEDA for consideration by the Committee on Tariff and Related Matters (CTRM), then a NEDA Board resolution formally adopts the amendments (Primer p.49).

124.question: When did the NEDA Board approve the adoption of the 2017 version of the AHTN?
124.reason: NEDA Board approval was on 27 June 2017, and the Philippines implemented AHTN 2017 starting 28 July 2017 (Primer p.49).

125.question: Which action did the Tariff Commission take to ensure the smooth implementation of AHTN 2017?

choices.A: Notified the Secretary of Finance and the BOC Commissioner of the non-validity of tariff classification rulings based on the old nomenclature
choices.C: Reduced all MFN rates to zero
choices.D: Removed the 8-digit level from the tariff lines

125.reason: Actions included notification to the Secretary of Finance and the BOC Commissioner, newspaper publication, transposition of MFN and FTA schedules, correlation tables, and publication of the Tariff Book (Primer pp.49-50).

126.question: The Supplementary Explanatory Notes (SEN) are:

choices.A: a list of FTA partners' tariff rates
choices.B: a compilation of the official interpretations of ASEAN subheadings, included in the AHTN 2017 publication
choices.C: a database of HS Committee classification decisions

126.reason: The SEN is a compilation of the official interpretations of ASEAN subheadings, included in the Tariff Administration and Policy AHTN 2017 publication (Primer p.50).

127.question: Per the Primer, when is the next cycle of review of the AHTN expected to be conducted?
127.reason: The WCO implements HS amendments every four to six years. Since the AHTN follows the HS, the next review is expected before 2022 (Primer p.50).

128.question: Tariff classification is:

choices.A: the act or process of assigning an appropriate HS or AHTN code to traded goods
choices.B: the computation of the dutiable value of goods
choices.C: the determination of the country of origin of goods

128.reason: Tariff classification is the act or process of assigning an appropriate HS or AHTN code to traded goods. It requires special skills and knowledge of products and classification rules (Primer p.51).

129.question: Which of the following is contained in an advance ruling on tariff classification?

choices.B: The CIF value of the goods
choices.C: The 8-digit AHTN code, applicable MFN and preferential rates, legal justification and validity period
choices.D: The name of the customs broker

129.reason: An AR contains a ruling number, date of issue, applicant's name and detailed description of the good, the 8-digit AHTN Code, applicable rates, legal justification and validity period (Primer p.51).

130.question: Faulty customs declarations caused by wrong tariff classification can result in:

choices.B: delays in clearance and release, overpayment of duties, and penalties including seizure

130.reason: Delays in clearance and release, overpayment of duties and other penalties, including seizure, can result from faulty customs declarations (Primer p.51).

131.question: Commission Order No. 2017-01 (Procedure on Application for an Advance Ruling) took effect on:
131.reason: The Order was published in The Manila Times on 20 September 2017 and took effect on 5 October 2017, fifteen days after publication (Primer pp.51-52, 60).

132.question: Commission Order No. 2017-01 was signed by Tariff Commission Chairperson Marilou P. Mendoza and approved by:

choices.A: Secretary of Finance Carlos G. Dominguez III

132.reason: The Order was approved by Secretary of Finance Carlos G. Dominguez III (Primer pp.51, 60).

133.question: An application for an advance ruling on tariff classification may cover:

choices.C: only one product or good, as determined by the Commission
choices.D: multiple goods under the same chapter

133.reason: An application for an AR shall cover only one product or good, as determined by the Commission (Primer pp.52, 56).

134.question: Under Section 1103 of the CMTA, an application for an advance ruling should be filed at least how many days before the date of importation or exportation?
134.reason: The application shall be filed at least ninety (90) days before the date of importation or exportation (Primer p.52).

135.question: How many copies of the filled-out application form must an applicant submit together with supporting documents and samples, if required?
135.reason: Applicants submit three (3) copies of the prescribed application form with supporting documents and samples, if required (Primer p.52).

136.question: Which of the following is NOT a ground for non-acceptance of an application for an advance ruling?

choices.A: The application was filed by an authorized representative
choices.B: The application is not in the prescribed form
choices.C: The application is filed less than ninety (90) days before importation or exportation

136.reason: An authorized representative may apply for an AR. Grounds for non-acceptance include wrong form, undeterminable classification, multiple goods, late filing and non-payment of fee (Primer pp.52, 56-57).

137.question: Within how many calendar days shall the Commission acknowledge receipt of the application and notify the applicant of the need for additional information and on-site verification?
137.reason: Within ten (10) calendar days the Commission acknowledges receipt and notifies the applicant. The applicant then has ten (10) calendar days to submit the information or allow verification (Primer pp.52, 57).

138.question: Pending the applicant's submission of additional information or on-site verification, what happens to the 30-day period to issue a ruling?

choices.B: It is suspended (the running of the period shall stay)

138.reason: Pending submission of additional information or on-site verification, the running of the 30-day period to issue a ruling shall stay (Primer pp.52, 57).

139.question: The Commission may NOT issue an advance ruling when:

choices.A: the applicant is a foreign exporter
choices.B: the goods are imported by sea
choices.C: the product is subject to an MFN rate
choices.D: the goods are subject of a pending court litigation, administrative review or appeal involving tariff classification

139.reason: Grounds for non-issuance include failure to give requested information, pending litigation or review involving tariff classification, no on-site verification, and misrepresentation (Primer pp.53, 57).

140.question: An advance ruling is effective from the date it is issued and is valid for:

choices.A: five (5) years from issuance, unless earlier revoked or modified due to changes in facts or circumstances

140.reason: The AR is valid for five (5) years from the date of issuance unless earlier revoked or modified (Primer pp.53, 58).

141.question: A modification of an advance ruling is of:
141.reason: An AR may be modified for an error, change in material facts, law or judicial decision, or policy. Modification is of prospective application (Primer pp.53, 58).

142.question: An advance ruling may be revoked by the Commission upon discovery of:

choices.A: a change in the MFN rate
choices.B: any false or misleading material information provided in the application
choices.C: a change in the importer's address
choices.D: a delay in the arrival of the goods

142.reason: The AR may be revoked upon discovery of any false or misleading material information, without prejudice to criminal, civil or administrative cases against the applicant (Primer pp.53, 58).

143.question: If the BOC deems an advance ruling adverse to the government, within how many days from receipt of a copy must it elevate the matter to the Secretary of Finance?
143.reason: The BOC shall, within five (5) days from receipt of a copy of the ruling, elevate it to the Secretary of Finance for review under Section 1128 of the CMTA (Primer p.58).

144.question: How soon must the Secretary of Finance automatically review the ruling, and what happens if no ruling is rendered within that period?

choices.A: Within 15 days of the BOC notice; the Commission's decision is deemed confirmed
choices.B: Within 30 days; the decision is deemed reversed
choices.C: Within 10 days; the decision is deemed modified
choices.D: Within 60 days; the decision is deemed confirmed

144.reason: The Secretary shall automatically review within 15 days from receipt of the BOC notice. If none is rendered, the Commission's decision is deemed confirmed (Primer p.58).

145.question: A motion for reconsideration of an advance ruling must be filed in writing within how many days from receipt, and how many motions are allowed?
145.reason: The applicant may file a motion within ten (10) days from receipt, on grounds such as mistake of fact, excusable negligence or newly discovered evidence. Only one motion is allowed (Primer p.59).

146.question: An appeal from the Commission's decision denying the motion for reconsideration may be filed before the Court of Tax Appeals within:
146.reason: An appeal may be filed before the Court of Tax Appeals within thirty (30) days from receipt of the decision denying the motion, or of the Secretary of Finance's decision (Primer p.59).

147.question: Under Commission Order No. 2017-01, requests for advance rulings on valuation and on rules of origin are filed with the:
147.reason: Requests for ARs on valuation (Sec. 1101) and rules of origin (Sec. 1102) are filed with the BOC. The Order also applies to goods moving into and from free zones (Primer p.54).

148.question: For purposes of Commission Order No. 2017-01, the date of importation shall be the date of:
148.reason: The date of importation shall be the date of lodgment of the goods declaration (Primer pp.55-56).

149.question: Unless otherwise provided, Commission Order No. 2017-01 shall be reviewed every:
149.reason: Section 10: the Order shall be reviewed every three (3) years and amended or revised, if necessary (Primer p.60).

150.question: Under Section 13, Commission Order No. 2017-01 takes effect how many days after its complete publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation?
150.reason: The Order takes effect fifteen (15) days after complete publication. Three certified copies go to the Office of the National Administrative Register of the UP Law Center (Primer p.60).

151.question: Under the Tariff Commission Primer, dumping is best described as what kind of practice?

choices.A: A form of price discrimination between two national markets
choices.B: A form of currency manipulation between two countries
choices.C: A customs valuation method for imported goods

151.reason: Dumping occurs when an exporter sells at a lower price in the importing market than in its own domestic market, or below cost of production (Primer p.61).

152.question: According to the Primer, is dumping always illegal under World Trade Organization rules?

choices.A: Yes, it is always illegal regardless of effect
choices.B: No, it is legal unless its injurious effect on the importing country's producers can be established
choices.C: Yes, but only for agricultural products
choices.D: No, it is never regulated by the WTO

152.reason: Dumping is legal under WTO rules unless its injurious effect on the importing country's producers can be established (Primer p.61).

153.question: A dumped import/product is introduced into the Philippines at what kind of price relative to its normal value?

choices.A: An export price equal to its normal value
choices.B: An export price higher than its normal value
choices.C: An export price less than its normal value in the ordinary course of trade
choices.D: A price fixed by the Bureau of Customs

153.reason: A dumped import/product refers to a product introduced into the Philippines at an export price less than its normal value in the ordinary course of trade (Primer p.61).

154.question: What is the difference between the export price and the normal value of a dumped product called?
154.reason: An anti-dumping duty is imposed on a dumped product, and the difference between the export price and the normal value of such product is the dumping margin (Primer p.61).

155.question: An anti-dumping measure, as defined in the Primer, is best described as what?

choices.A: A penalty imposed solely on foreign governments
choices.B: A trade remedy measure adopted by government to protect the domestic industry against dumping
choices.C: A subsidy given to domestic exporters
choices.D: A quota system on all imported goods

155.reason: An anti-dumping measure refers to a trade remedy measure adopted by government to protect the domestic industry against the unfair trade practice of dumping (Primer p.61).

156.question: What is Republic Act No. 8752 commonly known as, and when did it take effect?

choices.A: The Safeguard Measures Act, effective 1 January 2000
choices.B: The Customs Modernization Act, effective 4 September 1999
choices.C: The Anti-Dumping Act of 1999, effective 4 September 1999
choices.D: The Tariff and Customs Code, effective 12 August 1999

156.reason: Republic Act No. 8752, otherwise known as the Anti-Dumping Act of 1999, was signed on 12 August 1999 and took effect on 4 September 1999 (Primer p.62).

157.question: The provisions of Republic Act No. 8752 on anti-dumping protection were adopted in which section of the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act?
157.reason: The provisions of RA No. 8752 were adopted in Section 711 of the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (Primer p.62).

158.question: Aligning the Philippines' domestic anti-dumping law with which international instrument was part of the rationale for passing Republic Act No. 8752?

choices.A: The WTO Agreement on Anti-Dumping Practice (Article VI of GATT 1994)
choices.C: The ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement

158.reason: One rationale for RA No. 8752 was to align the domestic law with the WTO Agreement on Anti-Dumping Practice, Article VI of the GATT 1994 (Primer p.63).

159.question: When did the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 8752, issued as Joint Administrative Order No. 01, series of 2000, take effect?
159.reason: Joint Administrative Order No. 01, series of 2000, the IRR of RA No. 8752, took effect on 10 July 2000 (Primer p.63).

160.question: Tariff Commission Order No. 00-01, which governs the Commission's internal conduct of anti-dumping investigations, took effect on what date?
160.reason: Tariff Commission Order No. 00-01 took effect on 05 July 2000 (Primer p.63).

161.question: In administering anti-dumping legislation, which agency receives the properly documented application and determines whether a prima facie case exists?

choices.C: The Department of Agriculture or Department of Trade and Industry (Bureau of Import Services)

161.reason: The DA or DTI-BIS receives the properly documented application and determines whether a prima facie case exists to warrant initiation of an investigation (Primer p.63).

162.question: Which agency conducts the formal investigation and makes the final determination on the imposition of a definitive anti-dumping duty?

choices.C: The Department of Trade and Industry

162.reason: The Tariff Commission conducts the formal investigation and makes the final determination for purposes of imposing a definitive anti-dumping duty (Primer p.63).

163.question: Which agency is responsible for collecting anti-dumping duties once imposed?

choices.A: The Department of Trade and Industry

163.reason: The Bureau of Customs collects the anti-dumping duties (Primer p.63).

164.question: What must be true of a product's export price relative to its normal value for it to fall under the coverage of an anti-dumping investigation?

choices.A: The export price must be higher than the normal value
choices.B: The export price must be equal to the normal value
choices.C: The export price must be less than the normal value in the ordinary course of trade
choices.D: The export price must be set by the government of origin

164.reason: An anti-dumping investigation covers any product imported at an export price less than its normal value in the ordinary course of trade, causing or threatening material injury (Primer p.64).

165.question: A country of export, as defined in the Primer, is best described as what?

choices.A: The country where the product was manufactured regardless of shipment
choices.B: The country where the allegedly dumped product was shipped to the Philippines, regardless of the seller's location
choices.C: The country where the importer is registered
choices.D: The country that issued the certificate of origin

165.reason: A country of export is the country where the allegedly dumped product was shipped to the Philippines, regardless of the location of the seller (Primer p.64).

166.question: A country of origin, under the Primer's definition, is the country where what occurred?

choices.A: The product was shipped from, regardless of manufacture
choices.B: The product was wholly obtained or where the last substantial transformation took place
choices.C: The importer's head office is located
choices.D: The product was first offered for sale

166.reason: A country of origin is the country where the allegedly dumped product was either wholly obtained or where the last substantial transformation took place (Primer p.64).

167.question: Under the Primer, an agricultural product subject to anti-dumping rules is classified under which chapters of the Harmonized System?
167.reason: An agricultural product refers to a product classified under Chapters 1 to 24 of the Harmonized System, including those under Annex A (Primer p.64).

168.question: Non-agricultural or industrial goods that may be subject to anti-dumping measures are classified under which Harmonized System chapters?
168.reason: Non-agricultural or industrial goods refer to products classified under Chapters 25 to 97 of the HS and excluded from Annex A (Primer p.64).

169.question: Which of the following importations is exempted from an anti-dumping protest?

choices.A: Products imported by private traders for resale
choices.B: Products imported by or consigned to government agencies not organized for profit to stabilize or supplement shortages
choices.C: Products imported through a free port zone

169.reason: Products imported by or consigned to government agencies not organized for profit and designated to import, stabilize, or supplement shortages are exempted from anti-dumping protest (Primer p.64).

170.question: Who may file a written application for an anti-dumping protest under Republic Act No. 8752?

choices.C: Any person, whether natural or juridical, representing a domestic industry

170.reason: Any person, whether natural or juridical, representing a domestic industry, may file a written application using the proforma protestant's questionnaire (Primer p.64).

171.question: Within how many days must an applicant post the surety bond required under Republic Act No. 8752, failing which the application is dismissed?
171.reason: Failure to post the surety bond within ten (10) days results in the dismissal of the application (Primer p.65).

172.question: Which of the following is a factor considered in determining whether an anti-dumping application is frivolous?

choices.A: Whether the applicant is a large corporation
choices.B: Whether there is intentional misrepresentation of information or evidence supplied in the application
choices.C: Whether the applicant filed the case more than once
choices.D: Whether the product involved is agricultural

172.reason: A factor in determining whether an application is frivolous is whether there is any intentional misrepresentation of the information or evidence supplied (Primer p.65).

173.question: The term domestic industry, as used in anti-dumping investigations, generally refers to what?

choices.A: Only the single largest producer of the like product
choices.B: The domestic producers as a whole of the like product, or those whose collective output is a major proportion of total domestic production
choices.C: Only producers located in Metro Manila
choices.D: Only producers who export the like product

173.reason: Domestic industry refers to the domestic producers as a whole of the like product, or to those whose collective output constitutes a major proportion of total domestic production (Primer p.65).

174.question: What are the two thresholds of producer support needed for an anti-dumping protest to be accepted?

choices.A: Support from producers representing more than 50% of production, and support from producers accounting for at least 25% of production of the alleged dumped product
choices.B: Support from producers representing more than 75% of production only
choices.C: Support from at least three producers regardless of output
choices.D: Support from producers representing exactly 50% of production

174.reason: The thresholds require support by producers whose collective output is more than fifty percent (50%) of total production, and support by producers accounting for at least twenty-five percent (25%) of the product alleged to be dumped (Primer p.65).

175.question: Under what condition may an anti-dumping investigation be initiated without a written application from the domestic industry?

choices.A: Never, a written application is always mandatory
choices.B: In special circumstances, when the DA or DTI, on its own motion, has sufficient evidence of dumping, injury, and causal link
choices.C: Only when the exporter requests it
choices.D: Only upon order of the President

175.reason: In special circumstances, the DA or DTI may, on its own motion, initiate an anti-dumping investigation without a written application if there is sufficient evidence of dumping, injury, and a causal link (Primer p.65).

176.question: Which of the following must be included in a properly documented anti-dumping application under the Primer?

choices.A: A notarized waiver of appeal rights
choices.B: A complete description of the allegedly dumped product
choices.C: A certificate of good standing from the SEC
choices.D: A bank guarantee equal to the full value of imports

176.reason: Among the twelve required items, a properly documented application must contain a complete description of the allegedly dumped product (Primer p.66).

177.question: What must the applicant include at the end of a properly documented anti-dumping application?

choices.B: A certification signed by the applicant that the information presented is accurate and complete
choices.C: A copy of the applicant's business permit

177.reason: The application must include a certification signed by the applicant that the information presented is accurate and complete to the best of his knowledge (Primer p.66).

178.question: How many working days does the DA or DTI-BIS have to make a Prima Facie Determination upon acceptance of a properly documented protest?
178.reason: The DA or DTI-BIS has five (5) working days to decide whether the facts would constitute a dumping case (Primer p.67).

179.question: From receipt of answers to the questionnaire, how many working days does the DA or DTI-BIS have to make its Preliminary Determination on the imposition of a provisional anti-dumping duty?
179.reason: The DA or DTI-BIS has thirty (30) working days from receipt of the answers to the questionnaire to make its preliminary determination (Primer p.67).

180.question: How many days does the Tariff Commission have to complete its formal investigation and submit its report of findings for a Final Determination?
180.reason: The Commission has one hundred twenty (120) days from receipt of the advice from either the DA or DTI Secretary to complete its investigation and submit its report of findings (Primer p.67).

181.question: Within how many days from receipt of an affirmative final determination by the Tariff Commission must the DA or DTI Secretary issue a Department Order imposing an anti-dumping measure?
181.reason: Within ten (10) days from receipt of an affirmative final determination, the Secretary shall issue a Department Order for the imposition of an anti-dumping measure, unless an undertaking was earlier accepted (Primer p.67).

182.question: In case of a negative final determination, what happens to the anti-dumping bond posted by the importer?

choices.A: It is forfeited to the government
choices.B: It is immediately released to the importer after the appeal period to the Court of Tax Appeals lapses
choices.C: It is transferred to the domestic industry as damages
choices.D: It is held indefinitely by the Tariff Commission

182.reason: In case of a negative determination, an Order is issued for the Commissioner of Customs to immediately release the anti-dumping bond to the importer after the lapse of the appeal period to the Court of Tax Appeals (Primer p.67).

183.question: Where should the official request for the conduct of a formal anti-dumping investigation be secured, for industrial products?

choices.A: The Office of the Secretary of the Department of Trade and Industry
choices.D: The Office of the Secretary of the Department of Agriculture

183.reason: The Checklist of Requirements shows that for industrial products, the official request is secured from the DTI - Office of the Secretary (Primer p.67).

184.question: Under the Primer, an anti-dumping petition may be rejected or an investigation terminated if the provisionally estimated margin of dumping is less than what percentage of export price?
184.reason: A petition may be rejected if the provisionally estimated margin of dumping is less than two percent (2%) of export price (Primer p.68).

185.question: The volume of dumped imports from a particular country is normally regarded as negligible if it accounts for less than what percentage of total imports of the like article in the Philippines?
185.reason: The volume of dumped imports from a particular country shall normally be regarded as negligible if it accounts for less than three percent (3%) of imports of the like article (Primer p.68).

186.question: Before a final determination, how many days are interested parties given from receipt of the disclosed essential facts to defend their interests in writing?
186.reason: Parties are given five (5) days from the date of receipt of the essential facts to defend their interests in writing (Primer p.68).

187.question: What may investigating authorities do if exporting enterprises refuse to cooperate or provide incorrect or incomplete information during an investigation?

choices.B: Decide based on the best information available
choices.C: Impose the maximum possible duty automatically
choices.D: Refer the matter to the WTO immediately

187.reason: The authorities can decide based on the best information available when exporting enterprises refuse to cooperate or provide incorrect or incomplete information (Primer p.68).

188.question: Under the four elements of dumping, what does like product refer to?

choices.A: A product that is cheaper than the product under consideration
choices.B: A product identical or alike in all respects to the product under consideration, or one closely resembling it
choices.C: A product manufactured only in the Philippines
choices.D: A product that has never been imported before

188.reason: Like product refers to a product which is identical or alike in all respects to the product under consideration, or one with characteristics closely resembling it (Primer p.68).

189.question: The price difference or dumping margin element of dumping refers to what amount?

choices.A: The amount by which the export price exceeds the normal value
choices.B: The amount by which the normal value exceeds the export price
choices.C: The total customs duty paid on the import
choices.D: The shipping cost difference between countries

189.reason: Price difference/dumping margin is the amount by which the normal value exceeds the export price (selling price to an importer in the Philippines) (Primer p.68).

190.question: Material injury, as an element of dumping, includes which of the following?

choices.A: Only actual financial loss of a single company
choices.B: Material injury to a domestic industry, threat of material injury, or material retardation of the establishment of a domestic industry
choices.D: Only a decline in the exporter's profits

190.reason: Material injury means material injury to a domestic industry, threat of material injury, or material retardation of the establishment of a domestic industry (Primer p.68).

191.question: Causal link, as an element of dumping, refers to a finding of what?

choices.A: That the material injury suffered is the direct result of the importation of the dumped product
choices.B: That the exporter intended to cause harm
choices.C: That the domestic industry failed to modernize
choices.D: That the importer violated customs rules

191.reason: Causal link refers to a finding that the material injury suffered by the domestic industry is the direct result of the importation of the dumped product (Primer p.69).

192.question: Normal value, under the Primer, is best defined as what?

choices.A: The export price plus freight charges
choices.B: The comparable price at the date of sale of the like product in the ordinary course of trade in the country of export or origin
choices.C: The price set by the Philippine government for imports

192.reason: Normal value is the comparable price at the date of sale of the like product, commodity, or article in the ordinary course of trade when destined for consumption in the country of export or origin (Primer p.69).

193.question: A comparable price, for purposes of determining normal value, is normally assessed at what level of trade?
193.reason: A comparable price refers to the domestic price of the like product in the country of export or origin at the same level of trade, normally at the ex-factory level (Primer p.69).

194.question: An arm's length transaction refers to a transaction where the price is affected by what?

choices.C: Not affected by any relationship between the buyer and seller, or compensation, reimbursement, or other consideration

194.reason: An arm's length transaction refers to a transaction where the price is not affected by any relationship between the buyer and seller, or any compensation, reimbursement, benefit, or other consideration (Primer p.69).

195.question: A foreign producer's domestic selling price cannot be used as the basis for normal value if the volume of domestic sales is less than what percentage of export sales to the Philippines?
195.reason: One instance where domestic selling price cannot be used is when the volume of domestic sales is less than five percent (5%) of export sales to the Philippines (Primer p.69).

196.question: If a foreign producer's domestic selling price cannot be used, what may be used as an alternative basis for normal value?

choices.A: The price charged for the like product exported to an appropriate third country, or a constructed value based on production costs, GS&A, and profit
choices.B: The retail price in the Philippines
choices.C: The price set by the WTO Secretariat
choices.D: The average of all ASEAN country prices

196.reason: The normal value may be based on the comparable price charged for the like product exported to an appropriate third country, or the constructed value in the exporting country (Primer p.69).

197.question: Under the Primer, export price is defined as which of the following?

choices.A: The retail price in the country of destination
choices.B: The ex-factory price at the point of sale for export, or the FOB price at the point of shipment
choices.C: The price set by the importer's bank
choices.D: The landed cost including all duties

197.reason: Export price is (1) the ex-factory price at the point of sale for export, or (2) the FOB price at the point of shipment of the allegedly dumped product (Primer p.70).

198.question: When is an alternative export value used instead of the actual export price?

choices.B: When no export price is defined, or when it is unreliable due to a relationship or compensatory arrangement between the exporter and importer
choices.D: Only when the shipment exceeds a certain volume

198.reason: An alternative export value is used when no export price is defined, or when the export price is unreliable because of a relationship or compensatory arrangement (Primer p.70).

199.question: What may be used as the basis for an alternative export price?

choices.A: A constructed or deductive price based on the resale price to an independent buyer, less costs, or a reasonable price determined by the Secretary or the Commission
choices.B: The price listed in the exporter's catalog only
choices.C: The average retail price in the Philippines
choices.D: The original invoice price without adjustment

199.reason: An alternative export price may be based on a constructed or deductive price from the resale price to an independent buyer less costs, or a reasonable price determined by the Secretary or Commission (Primer p.70).

200.question: Which foreign exchange rate should generally be used in converting currencies for anti-dumping computations?

choices.A: The rate at the time of final determination
choices.B: The rate prevailing on the date of sale, unless the transaction is based on a forward contract rate
choices.C: The rate set by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas at year-end
choices.D: The average rate for the entire investigation period

200.reason: The exchange rate prevailing on the date of sale should be used, but if the transaction is based on an exchange rate stated in a forward contract, that rate should be used (Primer p.70).

201.question: In determining material injury to a domestic industry, authorities must objectively examine which of the following, among others?

choices.A: The political affiliation of the exporter
choices.B: The rate and amount of increase of dumped imports, relative to production or consumption

201.reason: Material injury determination requires objective examination of the rate and amount of increase of imports, among other factors, based on positive evidence (Primer p.70).

202.question: Price depression, as a modality in determining price effects of dumped imports, refers to what?

choices.A: The extent to which the domestic producer reduces his selling price to compete with the dumped product
choices.B: The extent to which dumped imports are seized by customs
choices.C: The extent to which the exporter raises prices
choices.D: The extent to which freight costs decrease

202.reason: Price depression refers to the extent to which the domestic producer reduces his selling price to compete with the allegedly dumped product (Primer p.71).

203.question: Price suppression refers to the extent to which dumped imports do what to the domestic producer?

choices.A: Increase the domestic producer's market share
choices.B: Prevent the domestic producer from increasing his selling price to a level allowing full cost recovery
choices.C: Force the domestic producer to export more
choices.D: Reduce the domestic producer's production capacity

203.reason: Price suppression refers to the extent by which dumped imports prevent the domestic producer from increasing the selling price to a level that allows full recovery of production costs (Primer p.71).

204.question: Price undercutting, as defined in the Primer, refers to what?

choices.A: The extent to which the dumped product is consistently sold at a price below the domestic selling price of the like product
choices.B: The extent to which import duties are reduced
choices.C: The extent to which exporters offer discounts to retailers
choices.D: The extent to which currency depreciates

204.reason: Price undercutting refers to the extent to which the allegedly dumped product is consistently sold at a price below the domestic selling price of the like product (Primer p.71).

205.question: A determination of threat of material injury must be based on what kind of evidence under the Primer?

choices.C: Facts, and not merely on allegation, conjecture, or remote possibility

205.reason: A determination of threat of material injury shall be based on facts and not merely on allegation, conjecture, or remote possibility (Primer p.71).

206.question: Which of the following is a factor considered in determining the existence of a threat of material injury?

choices.A: A significant rate of increase of dumped imports indicating likelihood of substantially increased importation
choices.B: The number of employees of the exporting company

206.reason: A significant rate of increase of the dumped imports in the domestic market, indicating the likelihood of substantially increased importation, is a factor in determining threat of material injury (Primer p.71).

207.question: In assessing other causes of injury not related to dumping, which is relevant evidence the authorities may consider?

choices.A: The volume and value of imported products not sold at dumping prices
choices.C: The number of trademarks registered by the exporter

207.reason: Relevant evidence for other causes of injury includes the volume and value of imported products not sold at dumping prices (Primer p.71).

208.question: Besides contraction in demand, which of the following is also examined as another cause of injury not related to dumping?

choices.C: The number of competing domestic brands
choices.D: The weather conditions in the exporting country

208.reason: Other relevant factors examined include trade restrictive practices and competition between foreign and domestic producers, and developments in technology (Primer p.72).

209.question: A provisional measure against dumping may take the form of what?

choices.B: A provisional duty or a security by cash deposit or bond equal to the estimated difference between normal value and export price
choices.C: A fine on the domestic industry
choices.D: A reduction of the MFN tariff rate

209.reason: A provisional measure takes the form of a provisional duty or, preferably, a security by cash deposit or bond equal to the estimated difference between the normal value and export price (Primer p.72).

210.question: A definitive anti-dumping duty is imposed following what kind of determination?
210.reason: A definitive anti-dumping duty is the final anti-dumping duty imposed on a protested product following an affirmative final determination (Primer p.72).

211.question: How long is a provisional anti-dumping measure generally imposed, and to what period may it be extended?

choices.A: Two months, extendable to four months
choices.B: Four months, extendable to six months upon request by exporters representing a significant percentage of the trade
choices.C: One year, extendable to two years
choices.D: Six months, extendable to twelve months

211.reason: A provisional measure is imposed for four (4) months, extendable to six (6) months upon request by exporters representing a significant percentage of the trade involved (Primer p.72).

212.question: A provisional anti-dumping duty lower than the provisionally estimated margin of dumping may be imposed for how long if deemed sufficient to remove or prevent material injury?
212.reason: A provisional anti-dumping duty lower than the provisionally estimated margin can be imposed for six (6) to nine (9) months if deemed sufficient to remove or prevent the material injury (Primer p.72).

213.question: What is the maximum duration of a definitive anti-dumping duty from the date of imposition?
213.reason: A definitive anti-dumping duty shall not exceed five (5) years from the date of imposition (Primer p.72).

214.question: A price undertaking, as defined in the Primer, is best described as what?

choices.A: A mandatory price ceiling imposed by the Tariff Commission
choices.B: A voluntary commitment by the exporter to increase his price or cease exporting at a dumped price
choices.C: A government subsidy to offset dumping losses
choices.D: A compulsory license to manufacture locally

214.reason: A price undertaking is a voluntary commitment by the exporter to increase his price or cease exporting to the Philippines at a dumped price, eliminating the material injury (Primer p.72).

215.question: A price undertaking is effective for what period unless the foreign exporter proves it is no longer necessary?
215.reason: Price undertaking is effective for a period of five (5) years unless the foreign exporter proves to the satisfaction of the authorities that it is no longer necessary (Primer p.72).

216.question: The lesser duty rule allows the imposition of an anti-dumping duty at what level?

choices.A: Always equal to the calculated margin of dumping
choices.B: Amounts lower than the calculated margin of dumping if adequate to remove the injury to the domestic industry
choices.C: Always double the calculated margin of dumping
choices.D: A fixed rate set by the WTO

216.reason: The lesser duty rule is the imposition of an anti-dumping duty in amounts lower than the calculated margin of dumping, if such lesser duty is adequate to remove the injury (Primer p.73).

217.question: The New Shipper's Review is conducted for what purpose?

choices.A: To determine individual margins of dumping for new exporters who did not export the product during the period of investigation
choices.B: To re-investigate the original domestic industry's finances
choices.C: To cancel an existing anti-dumping duty automatically
choices.D: To review the exporter's tax compliance

217.reason: The New Shipper's Review is carried out to determine individual margins of dumping for new exporters who have not exported the product during the period of investigation (Primer p.73).

218.question: How much time should have elapsed since the imposition of the anti-dumping duty before an Interim or Changed Circumstances Review can be initiated?
218.reason: At least one (1) year should have elapsed since the imposition of the anti-dumping duty before an interim review can be initiated (Primer p.73).
