219.question: A Sunset or Expiry Review is conducted before what milestone in the life of an anti-dumping duty?
219.reason: A Sunset or Expiry Review may be initiated before the sunset date, i.e., the 5th year, to determine whether expiry of the duty would lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping and injury (Primer p.73).

220.question: In the anti-dumping case involving Polypropylene resins from South Korea, what ultimately happened to the imposed measure?

choices.A: The measure remains permanently in force
choices.B: The measure was terminated after the Korean Government elevated the case to the WTO Dispute Settlement Body and an amicable settlement was reached
choices.C: The measure was increased after appeal
choices.D: The case was dismissed for lack of evidence

220.reason: The imposition of the measure on Polypropylene resins from South Korea was terminated after the Korean Government brought the case before the WTO Dispute Settlement Body and the parties agreed to an amicable settlement (Primer p.74).

221.question: What was the final determination in the anti-dumping case involving Cold rolled steel coils and sheet from Ukraine (2000)?

choices.B: Negative, due to negligible volume of imports
choices.D: Positive, but measure withheld for public interest

221.reason: The 2000 case on Cold rolled steel coils and sheet from Ukraine resulted in a Negative determination due to negligible volume of imports (Primer p.73).

222.question: What happened to the 2007 anti-dumping case on Sodium Tripolyphosphates from China?

choices.A: It resulted in a Positive determination with duty imposed
choices.B: The case was dismissed after the domestic industry withdrew its petition for expiry review and the parties settled amicably
choices.C: It was escalated to the WTO

222.reason: The Sodium Tripolyphosphates case against China was dismissed because the domestic industry withdrew its petition for expiry review and the parties settled the case amicably (Primer p.74).

223.question: What was the outcome of the 2010 anti-dumping case involving Mosquito Coil from Indonesia?

choices.B: Negative, due to a de minimis dumping margin
choices.C: Case dismissed for lack of standing
choices.D: Positive, but public interest exemption applied

223.reason: The 2010 Mosquito Coil case from Indonesia resulted in a Negative determination because of a de minimis dumping margin (Primer p.74).

224.question: What was the result of the 2001 anti-dumping case involving Clear figured glass from China?

choices.B: Negative, because dumping was not established
choices.D: Positive, but measure not imposed for public interest

224.reason: The 2001 Clear figured glass case against China resulted in a Negative determination because dumping was not established (Primer p.74).

225.question: What was the final determination for the 2014 anti-dumping case on Wheat flour from Turkey?
225.reason: The Table of Summary of Cases shows that the 2014 Wheat flour case from Turkey had a Positive final determination (Primer p.74).

226.question: A subsidy and countervailing measure, as defined in the Primer, is best described as what?

choices.B: A trade counter-measure adopted by government to offset a specific subsidy causing or threatening material injury to a domestic industry
choices.C: A quota restriction on agricultural imports

226.reason: A subsidy and countervailing measure is a trade counter-measure adopted by government to offset any specific subsidy given to exporters or manufacturers causing or threatening material injury to a domestic industry (Primer p.75).

227.question: Which of the following is given as an example of a financial contribution that may constitute a subsidy?

choices.A: A reduction in the exporter's shipping insurance
choices.B: Grants, soft loans, guarantees, and equity infusions provided by the government of the country of export or origin
choices.C: A private bank loan to a domestic importer
choices.D: A reduction in freight costs by a shipping line

227.reason: Examples of financial contributions constituting a subsidy include grants, soft loans, guarantees, certain equity infusions, tax credits, and goods or services provided by governments (Primer p.75).

228.question: Non-actionable or green subsidies are protected from countervailing action because they are considered what?

choices.B: Of particular value and not to be discouraged, or having no or minimal trade-distorting effects

228.reason: Non-actionable or green subsidies refer to subsidies protected from countervailing action because they are of particular value and not to be discouraged, or have no or minimal trade-distorting effects (Primer p.75).

229.question: For research assistance to foreign firms to qualify as a non-actionable subsidy, the assistance must not exceed what percentage of the costs of industrial research?
229.reason: Research assistance qualifies as non-actionable if it covers not more than seventy-five percent (75%) of the costs of industrial research, or fifty percent (50%) of pre-competitive development activity costs (Primer p.75).

230.question: For a region to be considered disadvantaged under the non-actionable subsidy criteria, its income or GDP per capita must not be above what percentage of the average for the territory concerned?
230.reason: One criterion is that income per capita, household income per capita, or GDP per capita must not be above eighty-five percent (85%) of the average for the territory concerned (Primer p.76).

231.question: For a region to be considered disadvantaged based on unemployment rate, that rate must be at least what percentage of the average, measured over a three-year period?
231.reason: The unemployment rate must be at least one hundred ten percent (110%) of the average for the territory concerned, measured over a three-year period (Primer p.76).

232.question: Assistance to promote adaptation of existing facilities to new environmental requirements, to qualify as non-actionable, must be limited to what percentage of the cost of adaptation?
232.reason: Environmental adaptation assistance must be limited to twenty percent (20%) of the cost of adaptation to qualify as non-actionable (Primer p.76).

233.question: Prohibited or red subsidies are generally contingent on what?

choices.B: Export performance, or the use of domestic over imported goods

233.reason: Prohibited subsidies or red subsidies include export subsidies contingent on export performance and subsidies contingent on the use of domestic over imported goods (Primer p.77).

234.question: Which of the following is listed as an example of a prohibited (red) subsidy?

choices.A: Export credits at rates below the government's cost of borrowing used to secure a material advantage
choices.B: A tax credit available to all domestic firms equally
choices.C: A publicly funded agricultural research program
choices.D: A regional development grant for disadvantaged areas

234.reason: Export credits at rates below the government's cost of borrowing, used to secure a material advantage in export credit terms, is listed as an example of a red subsidy (Primer p.77).

235.question: A specific subsidy, as defined in the Primer, refers to a subsidy limited to what?

choices.A: Only subsidies given to state-owned enterprises
choices.B: An enterprise or industry, or a group of enterprises or industries, or to certain regions
choices.C: Only subsidies for research and development
choices.D: Only subsidies exceeding a fixed peso amount

235.reason: A specific subsidy refers to a subsidy limited to an enterprise or industry, or a group of enterprises or industries, and can be limited to certain regions (Primer p.77).

236.question: Actionable or yellow subsidies are those that fall under what category?

choices.A: The definition of subsidy described in the Primer, without being prohibited or non-actionable
choices.B: Only subsidies given by international organizations
choices.D: Only subsidies granted after a countervailing investigation

236.reason: Actionable subsidies or yellow subsidies are those falling under the definition of subsidy described in the Primer (Primer p.78).

237.question: A subsidized import/product is one that is granted a subsidy and that does what to a domestic industry?

choices.A: Has no effect on the domestic industry
choices.B: Causes or threatens to cause material injury, or materially retards growth or establishment of the domestic industry

237.reason: A subsidized import/product is one causing or threatening to cause material injury to a domestic industry, or materially retarding the growth or establishment of a domestic industry (Primer p.78).

238.question: What is Republic Act No. 8751 commonly known as, and when did it take effect?

choices.A: The Anti-Dumping Act of 1999, effective 4 September 1999
choices.B: An Act Strengthening the Mechanisms for the Imposition of Countervailing Duties, effective 31 August 1999
choices.C: The Tariff Reform Program, effective 1 January 2000
choices.D: The Customs Modernization Act, effective 31 August 1999

238.reason: RA No. 8751, which strengthens the mechanisms for imposing countervailing duties on subsidized imports, was signed on 7 August 1999 and took effect on 31 August 1999 (Primer p.78).

239.question: The provisions of Republic Act No. 8751 on countervailing duties were adopted in which section of the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act?
239.reason: The provisions of RA No. 8751 were adopted in Section 713 of the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (Primer p.78).

240.question: When did the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 8751, issued as Joint Administrative Order No. 02, series of 2000, take effect?
240.reason: Joint Administrative Order No. 02, series of 2000, the IRR of RA No. 8751, took effect on 25 September 2000 (Primer p.78).

241.question: Aligning the domestic countervailing duty law with which international agreement was part of the rationale for passing Republic Act No. 8751?

choices.A: The WTO Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures (Article XVI of GATT 1994)

241.reason: One rationale for RA No. 8751 was to align the domestic law with the WTO Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures, Article XVI of GATT 1994 (Primer p.78).

242.question: In administering countervailing legislation, which agency receives the properly documented application and conducts the preliminary investigation?
242.reason: The DA or DTI-BIS receives the properly documented application, determines whether a prima facie case exists, and conducts the preliminary investigation (Primer p.78).

243.question: Which agency conducts the formal investigation and makes the final determination for imposing a definitive countervailing duty?

choices.A: The Department of Trade and Industry
choices.D: The National Economic and Development Authority

243.reason: The Tariff Commission conducts the formal investigation and makes the final determination for purposes of imposing the definitive countervailing duty (Primer p.79).

244.question: Which agency collects countervailing duties once imposed?

choices.B: The Department of Trade and Industry

244.reason: The Bureau of Customs collects the countervailing duties (Primer p.79).

245.question: A countervailing duty protest applies to any product that is granted what, by the government of the country of export or origin?

choices.B: Any kind or form of specific subsidy upon exportation or manufacture, causing or threatening material injury

245.reason: A countervailing duty protest applies to a product granted, directly or indirectly, any kind or form of specific subsidy upon exportation or manufacture, causing or threatening material injury to a domestic industry (Primer p.79).

246.question: In countervailing cases, a country of export refers to what?

choices.A: The country where the product was manufactured
choices.B: The country from where the allegedly subsidized product was shipped to the Philippines, regardless of the seller's location
choices.C: The country where the subsidy program was enacted into law
choices.D: The country of the buyer's citizenship

246.reason: A country of export is the country from where the allegedly subsidized product was shipped to the Philippines, regardless of the location of the seller (Primer p.79).

247.question: In countervailing cases, a country of origin refers to what?

choices.A: Where the allegedly subsidized product was wholly obtained or where the last substantial transformation took place
choices.B: Where the product was first advertised
choices.C: Where the importer's business is registered
choices.D: Where the shipping vessel is flagged

247.reason: A country of origin is where the allegedly subsidized product was either wholly obtained or where the last substantial transformation took place (Primer p.79).

248.question: For countervailing purposes, an agricultural product that may be subsidized is classified under which Harmonized System chapters?
248.reason: An agricultural product refers to a product classified under Chapters 1 to 24 of the HS, including specific tariff lines under Annex A (Primer p.79).

249.question: For countervailing purposes, non-agricultural or industrial goods that may be subsidized are classified under which Harmonized System chapters?
249.reason: Non-agricultural or industrial goods refer to products classified under Chapters 25 to 97 of the HS and excluded from Annex A (Primer p.79).

250.question: Which importations are exempted from countervailing duty protest?

choices.A: Articles imported by or consigned to government agencies not organized for profit to stabilize or supplement shortages, and conditionally duty-free importations under Section 800 of the CMTA
choices.B: Articles imported by private corporations for resale
choices.C: Articles imported during an election period
choices.D: Articles imported by foreign embassies only

250.reason: Exempted importations include articles imported by or consigned to government agencies not organized for profit to stabilize or supplement shortages, and conditionally duty-free importations under Section 800 of the CMTA (Primer p.80).

251.question: To whom should a verified petition for countervailing action on industrial goods be filed?

choices.B: The Secretary of Trade and Industry

251.reason: A verified petition requesting imposition of a countervailing duty on industrial goods is filed with the Secretary of Trade and Industry (Primer p.80).

252.question: In countervailing investigations, the term domestic industry may exclude producers who are related to exporters or importers, or who are themselves importers of what?

choices.A: Raw materials used by the domestic industry
choices.B: The allegedly subsidized product or a like product from other countries

252.reason: The term domestic industry may be interpreted as referring to the rest of the producers when producers are related to exporters/importers or are themselves importers of the allegedly subsidized product or a like product from other countries (Primer p.80).

253.question: What are the two thresholds of producer support needed for a countervailing petition to be accepted?

choices.A: Support from producers representing more than 50% and support from producers accounting for at least 25% of total production of the like product
choices.B: Support from exactly two producers regardless of output
choices.C: Support from producers representing more than 90% of total production
choices.D: Support from the government agency alone

253.reason: The thresholds require support by producers whose collective output is more than fifty percent (50%), and support by producers accounting for at least twenty-five percent (25%) of total production of the like product (Primer p.80).

254.question: Under what condition may a countervailing investigation be initiated without a written application from the domestic industry?

choices.B: In special circumstances, when the DA or DTI, on its own motion, has sufficient evidence of subsidy, injury, and causal link
choices.C: Only at the request of the foreign government

254.reason: In special circumstances, the DA or DTI may, on its own motion, initiate a countervailing action even without a written application, if there is sufficient evidence of subsidy, injury, and causal link (Primer p.81).

255.question: A properly documented countervailing application must contain information on what, regarding the alleged subsidy?

choices.B: The nature, extent, and estimated amount of the subsidy in question

255.reason: Among the required items, a properly documented countervailing application must state the nature, extent, and estimated amount of the subsidy in question (Primer p.81).

256.question: Which of the following must also be included in a properly documented countervailing application, relating to the shipment itself?

choices.A: The estimated aggregate or cumulative quantity, the port, and the date of arrival, and the import entry declaration of the allegedly subsidized product

256.reason: The application must include the estimated aggregate or cumulative quantity, the port, and the date of arrival, and the import entry declaration of the allegedly subsidized product (Primer p.81).

257.question: A properly documented countervailing application must also disclose what information about the domestic industry's workforce?

choices.B: The number of persons employed by the affected domestic industry

257.reason: The application must state the number of persons employed by the affected domestic industry (Primer p.81).

258.question: Under the Primer, what is the purpose of government-to-government consultations in a countervailing case?

choices.A: To negotiate a new free trade agreement
choices.B: To clarify the situation on matters in the application and arrive at a mutually agreed solution with the government of the country of export or origin
choices.C: To determine the exchange rate for duty computation
choices.D: To settle disputes between competing domestic producers

258.reason: The DA or DTI Secretary notifies the government of the country of export or origin about the impending application and invites consultation to clarify matters and arrive at a mutually agreed upon solution (Primer p.83).

259.question: When must government-to-government consultations in a countervailing case be conducted?

choices.A: After the final determination is issued
choices.B: Only if the importer requests it
choices.C: Upon acceptance of a properly documented application and before initiating an investigation
choices.D: Only during the formal investigation by the Tariff Commission

259.reason: Consultations are conducted upon acceptance of a properly documented application and before initiating an investigation (Primer p.83).

260.question: For a product originating from a developed country, a countervailing petition may be rejected if the amount of subsidy is de minimis, meaning less than what percentage ad valorem of export price?
260.reason: For a developed country, the subsidy is considered de minimis if it is less than one per cent (1%) ad valorem as a percentage of export price (Primer p.83).

261.question: For a product originating from a developing country, what is the de minimis subsidy threshold, and what is it for least developed countries?

choices.A: Two percent (2%) for developing countries and three percent (3%) for least developed countries
choices.C: Five percent (5%) for developing countries and ten percent (10%) for least developed countries
choices.D: Three percent (3%) for developing countries and two percent (2%) for least developed countries

261.reason: For developing countries the de minimis threshold is two per cent (2%), and for least developed countries it is three per cent (3%) (Primer p.83).

262.question: For a product from a developing country, the volume of imports is considered negligible if it accounts for less than what percentage of total imports of the product, unless such countries collectively account for more than nine percent?
262.reason: The volume of imports from a developing country is considered negligible if it accounts for less than four per cent (4%) of total imports, unless such countries collectively account for more than nine per cent (9%) (Primer p.83).

263.question: In a countervailing investigation, before making the final determination, the Tariff Commission is required to disclose essential facts to which of the following parties?

choices.B: The domestic industry, exporters or foreign producers, their governments, and importers

263.reason: Before the final determination, the Tariff Commission must disclose to interested parties, such as the domestic industry, exporters or foreign producers, their governments, and importers, the essential facts on which the decision is based (Primer p.83).

264.question: If exporting enterprises in a countervailing investigation refuse to cooperate or provide incorrect or incomplete information, what may the investigating authorities do?

choices.A: Automatically impose the maximum countervailing duty allowed
choices.B: Decide based on the best information available
choices.D: Refer the matter directly to the WTO Dispute Settlement Body

264.reason: The authorities can decide based on the best information available if exporting enterprises refuse to cooperate, impede the investigation, or provide incorrect or incomplete information (Primer p.84).

265.question: What are the four elements that must be established for countervailing, according to the Primer?

choices.A: Like product, subsidy, material injury, and causal link
choices.B: Like product, dumping margin, material injury, and causal link
choices.C: Subsidy, export price, normal value, and causal link
choices.D: Like product, tariff classification, subsidy, and injury

265.reason: The four elements of countervailing are like product, subsidy, material injury, and causal link (Primer p.84).

266.question: In a countervailing investigation, a determination of injury must be based on positive evidence and involve an objective examination of which two matters?

choices.A: The volume of subsidized imports' effect on prices in the domestic market, and the consequent impact on domestic producers
choices.B: The exporter's tax returns and shipping manifests
choices.C: The importer's profit margin and the exporter's employee count
choices.D: The exchange rate trend and the shipping insurance cost

266.reason: A determination of injury shall be based on positive evidence and involve an objective examination of the volume of subsidized imports on prices in the domestic market and the consequent impact of these imports on domestic producers (Primer p.84).

267.question: Price depression, as a modality in determining price effects of subsidized imports, refers to what?

choices.A: The extent to which the exporter increases subsidy amounts
choices.B: The extent to which the domestic producer reduces his selling price to compete with the allegedly subsidized product
choices.C: The extent to which currency appreciates
choices.D: The extent to which freight rates decrease

267.reason: Price depression refers to the extent to which the domestic producer reduces his selling price to compete with the allegedly subsidized product (Primer p.85).

268.question: Price suppression, in the context of subsidized imports, refers to what?

choices.A: The extent by which the subsidized product prevents the domestic producer from increasing his selling price to a level allowing full cost recovery
choices.B: The extent to which the subsidized product is banned from entry
choices.C: The extent to which the domestic producer raises export volumes
choices.D: The extent to which the government grants tax holidays

268.reason: Price suppression refers to the extent by which the allegedly subsidized product prevents the domestic producer from increasing his selling price to a level allowing full recovery of production costs (Primer p.85).

269.question: Price undercutting, in a countervailing context, refers to what?

choices.A: The extent to which the subsidized product is consistently sold at a price below the domestic selling price of the like product
choices.B: The extent to which the government recovers subsidy costs
choices.C: The extent to which import duties increase
choices.D: The extent to which the exporter's profit margin shrinks

269.reason: Price undercutting refers to the extent to which the allegedly subsidized product is consistently sold at a price below the domestic selling price of the like product (Primer p.85).

270.question: Which of the following is a factor considered in determining the existence of a threat of material injury in a countervailing investigation?

choices.A: The nature of the subsidy in question and the trade effects likely to arise therefrom
choices.C: The number of patents held by the exporter

270.reason: A factor in determining threat of material injury is the nature of the subsidy in question and the trade effects likely to arise therefrom (Primer p.85).

271.question: Which of the following is listed as an example of an injury factor not related to subsidization, under the Primer?

choices.A: Volumes and prices of non-subsidized imports of the product, commodity, or article in question
choices.D: The amount of the subsidy granted

271.reason: Examples of injury factors not related to subsidization include the volumes and prices of non-subsidized imports of the product, commodity, or article in question (Primer p.85).

272.question: Aside from contraction in demand, which of the following is also listed as an injury factor not related to subsidization?

choices.C: The number of subsidy programs in the exporting country

272.reason: Injury factors not related to subsidization also include developments in technology, along with trade restrictive practices and export performance of the domestic industry (Primer p.86).

273.question: A provisional measure against subsidization takes the form of a security equal to what amount, and when may it be applied?

choices.A: The full value of the shipment, applied immediately upon filing of the petition
choices.B: The provisionally calculated amount of subsidy, applied only after an affirmative preliminary determination and no sooner than 60 days from initiation of the case
choices.C: A fixed peso amount set by the Bureau of Customs
choices.D: Double the amount of the alleged subsidy, applied at any time during the investigation

273.reason: A provisional measure takes the form of a security (cash deposit or bond) equal to the provisionally calculated amount of subsidy, applied only after an affirmative preliminary determination and no sooner than 60 days from initiation of the case (Primer p.86).

274.question: What is the maximum duration of a provisional countervailing measure?
274.reason: A provisional countervailing measure shall not exceed four (4) months (Primer p.86).

275.question: What is the maximum duration of a definitive countervailing duty from the date of imposition?
275.reason: A definitive countervailing duty shall not exceed five (5) years from the date of imposition (Primer p.86).

276.question: A voluntary undertaking in a countervailing case may take the form of what?

choices.A: A unilateral tariff reduction by the Philippines
choices.B: An offer by the exporting government to eliminate or limit the subsidy, or a commitment by the foreign exporter or producer to increase prices or cease exporting at the subsidized price
choices.C: A loan guarantee extended by the Bureau of Customs
choices.D: A request by the domestic industry to withdraw its petition

276.reason: Voluntary undertaking is an offer by the exporting government to eliminate or limit the subsidy, or a voluntary commitment by the foreign exporter/producer to increase prices or cease exporting at the subsidized price (Primer p.86).

277.question: A voluntary undertaking offer in a countervailing case may only be made after what has occurred?

choices.B: A preliminary affirmative determination of subsidization and injury to the domestic industry
choices.C: The lapse of the five-year duty period
choices.D: The filing of the original petition

277.reason: An offer of price undertaking shall be made only after a preliminary affirmative determination of subsidization and injury to the domestic industry has been reached (Primer p.86).

278.question: How long is a price undertaking in a countervailing case effective, unless the foreign exporter proves it is no longer necessary?
278.reason: Price undertaking is effective for a period of five (5) years unless the foreign exporter proves to the satisfaction of the authorities that it is no longer necessary (Primer p.86).

279.question: An Interim or Changed Circumstances Review of a countervailing duty may be initiated by whom?

choices.B: The Commission motu proprio, or upon direction of the Secretary, or upon petition of any interested party

279.reason: The Interim or Changed Circumstances Review is conducted by the Commission motu proprio, or upon the direction of the Secretary, or upon petition of any interested party (Primer p.86).

280.question: How much time must have elapsed since the imposition of a countervailing duty before an Interim Review can be initiated?
280.reason: At least one (1) year should have elapsed since the imposition of the countervailing duty before an interim review can be initiated (Primer p.86).

281.question: A Sunset or Expiry Review of a countervailing duty may be initiated before what point in the duty's lifespan?

choices.B: The sunset date, i.e., the 5th year

281.reason: A Sunset or Expiry Review may be initiated by any interested party or upon the Commission's own motion before the sunset date, i.e., the 5th year (Primer p.86).

282.question: According to the Primer, how many countervailing cases has the Tariff Commission formally investigated under Republic Act No. 8751 since it took effect?

choices.A: Three cases, all resulting in positive determinations
choices.B: None; no case has been endorsed to the Tariff Commission for formal investigation
choices.D: One case, which is still pending

282.reason: Since RA No. 8751 took effect in August 1999, no case has been endorsed to the Tariff Commission for formal investigation (Primer p.87).

283.question: According to the Primer, safeguard measures are trade remedy measures adopted by government for what purpose?

choices.A: To offset a specific subsidy granted by a foreign government
choices.B: To protect a specific domestic industry from an increase in imports causing or threatening to cause serious injury to the industry
choices.C: To penalize exporters who dump products below normal value
choices.D: To regulate currency exchange rates on imports

283.reason: Safeguard measures are trade remedy measures adopted by government to protect a specific domestic industry from an increase in imports causing, or threatening to cause, serious injury to the industry (Primer p.87).

284.question: A general safeguard measure is imposed against imports under what kind of conditions?

choices.A: When products are imported in increased quantities, absolute or relative to domestic production, causing or threatening serious injury
choices.B: Only when the exporter fails to pay export duties
choices.C: Only when imports originate from a single specific country
choices.D: Only when the product is classified as agricultural

284.reason: A general safeguard measure is imposed against imports if the products are being imported in increased quantities, either absolute or relative to domestic production, causing or threatening serious injury (Primer p.87).

285.question: A special safeguard measure under the Primer is imposed against which products, and what symbol are they designated with?

choices.B: Agricultural products whose quantitative restrictions were tariffied and designated with the symbol 'SSG' in the GATT Schedule of Concessions

285.reason: A special safeguard measure is imposed against importations of agricultural products whose quantitative import restrictions were converted into ordinary customs duties and designated with the symbol SSG in the GATT Schedule of Concessions (Primer p.87).

286.question: A special safeguard measure may be invoked if which of the following conditions is met?

choices.A: The cumulative import volume each year exceeds its trigger volume, or the actual CIF import price is less than its trigger price
choices.B: The exporter fails to disclose its subsidy program
choices.C: The domestic industry files for bankruptcy
choices.D: The importer fails to pay customs duties on time

286.reason: A special safeguard measure may be invoked if the cumulative import volume each year exceeds its trigger volume, or, not concurrently, if the actual CIF import price is less than its trigger price (Primer p.87).

287.question: For a special safeguard measure, must injury to the domestic industry be established?

choices.A: Yes, injury must always be established first
choices.B: No, injury to the domestic industry need not be established in either case
choices.C: Only if the trigger volume is exceeded by more than 50%

287.reason: For a special safeguard measure, in either case (trigger volume or trigger price), injury to the domestic industry need not be established (Primer p.87).

288.question: What is Republic Act No. 8800 commonly known as, and when did it take effect?

choices.A: The Safeguard Measures Act, effective 9 August 2000
choices.C: The Countervailing Duty Act, effective 31 August 1999
choices.D: The Customs Modernization Act, effective 1 January 2000

288.reason: RA No. 8800, otherwise known as the Safeguard Measures Act, was signed on 19 July 2000 and took effect on 9 August 2000 (Primer p.87).

289.question: The provisions of Republic Act No. 8800 on safeguard measures were adopted in which section of the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act?
289.reason: The provisions of RA No. 8800 were adopted in Section 712 of the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (Primer p.87).

290.question: Aligning the domestic safeguards law with which international agreements was part of the rationale for passing Republic Act No. 8800?

choices.A: The WTO Agreement on Safeguards (GATT Article XIX) and the WTO Agreement on Agriculture
choices.C: The Kyoto Convention and the Harmonized System Convention
choices.D: The ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement only

290.reason: One rationale for RA No. 8800 was to align the domestic law with the WTO Agreement on Safeguards (GATT Article XIX) and the WTO Agreement on Agriculture (Primer p.89).

291.question: When did the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 8800, issued as Joint Administrative Order No. 03, series of 2000, take effect?
291.reason: Joint Administrative Order No. 03, series of 2000, the IRR of RA No. 8800, took effect on 11 October 2000 (Primer p.89).

292.question: Tariff Commission Order No. 00-02, governing the Commission's internal conduct of safeguard investigations, took effect on what date?
292.reason: Tariff Commission Order No. 00-02 took effect on 05 July 2000 (Primer p.89).

293.question: In administering a general safeguard measure, which agency decides on the form of the measure to impose and issues the Department Order?

choices.B: The Secretary of either the DA or DTI, as applicable
choices.D: The National Economic and Development Authority

293.reason: The Secretary of either Department decides on the form of safeguard measure to impose and issues a Department Order implementing it, pursuant to the results of the preliminary and formal investigation (Primer p.89).

294.question: For a special safeguard measure on sensitive agricultural products, within how many working days from receipt of the petition must the Department of Agriculture make its finding?
294.reason: The DA makes its finding within five (5) working days from receipt of the petition for a special safeguard measure (Primer p.89).

295.question: For a general safeguard measure, a petition filed with the Secretary of Agriculture or Secretary of Trade and Industry, upon affirmative preliminary findings, is endorsed to which body for formal investigation?
295.reason: Upon affirmative preliminary findings by the Secretary, the case for a general safeguard measure is endorsed to the Tariff Commission for formal investigation (Primer p.90).

296.question: For a special safeguard measure, what may any person, whether natural or juridical, request?

choices.A: A verification of whether a particular agricultural product can be imposed a special safeguard duty
choices.B: A reduction in the MFN tariff rate
choices.C: An advance ruling on tariff classification
choices.D: A refund of previously paid customs duties

296.reason: For a special safeguard measure, any person, whether natural or juridical, may request a verification if a particular agricultural product can be imposed a special safeguard duty (Primer p.90).

297.question: Under what circumstance may the DA or DTI Secretary initiate a safeguard investigation on his own motion, without a written application from the domestic industry?

choices.A: Never, a written application is always required
choices.B: In special circumstances, where there is evidence that increased imports are a substantial cause of, or threaten to substantially cause, serious injury
choices.C: Only upon instruction of a foreign government
choices.D: Only during a declared state of emergency

297.reason: In special circumstances, the DA or DTI Secretary may, on his own motion, initiate a preliminary safeguard investigation if there is evidence that increased imports are a substantial cause of, or threaten to substantially cause, serious injury (Primer p.91).

298.question: Aside from the Secretary's own motion, a safeguard investigation may also be initiated upon the request of whom?

choices.A: The President, or a resolution of the House of Representatives or Senate Committee on Agriculture, or the HOR or Senate Committee on Trade and Commerce
choices.C: Only the Bureau of Internal Revenue
choices.D: Only a private law firm representing importers

298.reason: The Secretary may also initiate action upon the request of the President, or a resolution of the House of Representatives or Senate Committee on Agriculture, or HOR or Senate Committee on Trade and Commerce (Primer p.91).

299.question: A properly documented safeguard petition must include a complete description of the imported product specifying what, among other details?

choices.A: The HS Code under which the product is classified, and the present MFN and preferential tariff rates
choices.C: The buyer's personal tax identification number
choices.D: The vessel's registry and flag state

299.reason: A safeguard petition must contain a complete description of the imported product specifying the HS Code under which it is classified and the present tariff rates, both MFN and preferential (Primer p.91).

300.question: How many years of import volume and value data preceding the date of application must a safeguard petition generally include?
300.reason: The petition must include information on the volume and value of imports for the last five (5) years preceding the date of application (Primer p.91).

301.question: In the Prima Facie Determination stage for a general safeguard measure, how many calendar days does the DA or DTI-BIS have to decide whether a prima facie case exists?
301.reason: Upon acceptance of a properly documented petition, the DA or DTI-BIS has five (5) calendar days to decide whether a prima facie case exists to merit initiation of a preliminary investigation (Primer p.91).

302.question: In the Preliminary Determination stage for a general safeguard measure, how many calendar days does the DA or DTI-BIS have to decide whether to impose a provisional safeguard measure?
302.reason: The DA or DTI-BIS has thirty (30) calendar days from receipt of the properly documented application or a motu proprio initiation to make its preliminary determination on imposing a provisional safeguard measure (Primer p.91).

303.question: In the Final Determination stage, how many calendar days does the Tariff Commission have to conclude its formal investigation, and how many if the Secretary certifies the case as urgent?

choices.A: 120 calendar days, or 60 days if certified urgent
choices.B: 90 calendar days, or 45 days if certified urgent
choices.C: 60 calendar days, or 30 days if certified urgent
choices.D: 150 calendar days, or 90 days if certified urgent

303.reason: The Tariff Commission has 120 calendar days (or 60 days if the Secretary certifies the case as urgent) from receipt of the endorsement to conclude its formal investigation and submit its report (Primer p.92).

304.question: In the Issuance of Department Order stage, how many calendar days does the Secretary have from receipt of the Commission's report to decide on the level and form of the safeguard measure?
304.reason: The Secretary has fifteen (15) calendar days from receipt of the Commission's report of findings and recommendation to decide on the level and form of the safeguard measure, if the determination is affirmative (Primer p.92).

305.question: In case of a negative determination in a general safeguard investigation, what does the Secretary authorize through the Secretary of Finance?

choices.A: The forfeiture of the cash bond to the government
choices.B: The return of the cash bond previously collected to the importer
choices.C: The transfer of the cash bond to the domestic industry
choices.D: The conversion of the cash bond into a permanent duty

305.reason: In case of a negative determination, the Secretary issues a Department Order terminating the case and a written instruction to the BOC Commissioner, through the Secretary of Finance, authorizing the return of the cash bond previously collected (Primer p.92).

306.question: Under the formal investigation checklist for a general safeguard measure, where is the required Adjustment Plan secured?

choices.A: From the publisher of two newspapers of general circulation
choices.B: From the petitioner or the domestic producer(s)

306.reason: Table 3.4 shows that the Adjustment Plan is secured from the petitioner or domestic producer(s) (Primer p.93).

307.question: Under the elements for imposition of a general safeguard measure, what does a like product refer to?

choices.A: A domestic product identical, i.e., alike in all respects, to the imported product under consideration, or one with closely resembling characteristics
choices.B: Any product imported from an MFN country
choices.C: A product that competes only in export markets
choices.D: A product with the same HS Code regardless of characteristics

307.reason: A like product shall mean a domestic product which is identical, i.e., alike in all respects, to the imported product under consideration, or one with characteristics closely resembling it (Primer p.93).

308.question: Under the Primer, directly competitive products in a safeguard investigation shall mean what?

choices.C: Products imported under a preferential tariff rate
choices.D: Products subject to an existing anti-dumping duty

308.reason: Directly competitive products shall mean domestically produced substitutable products (Primer p.93).

309.question: For purposes of establishing increased imports in a safeguard case, what characteristics must the increase have?

choices.A: It must be gradual, minor, and long-term
choices.B: It must be recent, sharp, and significant
choices.C: It must exceed 50% of total domestic production
choices.D: It must originate from a single exporting country

309.reason: Increased imports may be either in absolute terms or relative to domestic production; the increase should be recent, sharp, and significant (Primer p.93).

310.question: Serious injury, as defined in the Primer's safeguard provisions, means what kind of impairment?

choices.A: Any decline in profit, however minor
choices.B: A significant impairment in the position of a domestic industry after evaluation of all relevant factors of an objective and quantifiable nature
choices.C: A temporary reduction in exports only
choices.D: A reduction in the number of competitors in the market

310.reason: Serious injury shall mean a significant impairment in the position of a domestic industry after evaluation by competent authorities of all relevant factors of an objective and quantifiable nature (Primer p.93).

311.question: How is a threat of serious injury understood under the Primer's safeguard provisions?

choices.A: As serious injury that is imminent
choices.B: As a mere allegation by the domestic industry
choices.C: As any decline in export volume
choices.D: As a hypothetical future scenario with no evidentiary basis

311.reason: Threat of serious injury shall be understood to mean serious injury that is imminent (Primer p.93).

312.question: Causality, as an element for a general safeguard measure, refers to what overall assessment?

choices.A: That the serious injury suffered by the domestic industry is the direct result of increased imports of the product under consideration
choices.B: That the exporter acted in bad faith
choices.C: That the domestic industry failed to innovate
choices.D: That the importer violated the CMTA

312.reason: Causality refers to the overall assessment that the serious injury suffered by the domestic industry is the direct result of increased imports of the product under consideration (Primer p.93).

313.question: Among the economic factors the Secretary and Commission consider in determining serious injury, which of the following is included?

choices.A: Significant idling of productive facilities, including closure of plants or underutilization of production capacity
choices.C: The number of trademarks filed by competitors

313.reason: In determining serious injury, the Secretary and Commission consider economic factors including significant idling of productive facilities, including closure of plants or underutilization of production capacity (Primer p.94).

314.question: Which of the following is a factor in determining the existence of a threat of serious injury in a general safeguard case?

choices.A: A significant rate of increase in imports evidenced by letters of credit, supply or sales contracts, or the award of a tender
choices.B: The exporter's compliance with environmental regulations
choices.C: The number of patents filed by the domestic industry

314.reason: A significant rate of increase in imports into the Philippines, evidenced inter alia by letters of credit, supply or sales contracts, the award of a tender, or an irrevocable offer, is a factor in determining threat of serious injury (Primer p.94).

315.question: In the case of non-agricultural products, before a provisional general safeguard measure in the form of a tariff increase may be imposed, what must the Secretary first establish?

choices.A: That the measure is in the public interest
choices.B: That the exporter has agreed to the measure
choices.C: That the WTO has approved the measure
choices.D: That a bilateral agreement exists with the exporting country

315.reason: For non-agricultural products, the Secretary shall first establish that imposition of the provisional safeguard measure would be in the public interest (Primer p.94).

316.question: Which of the following is one of the forms a definitive general safeguard measure may take?

choices.A: A decrease in or imposition of a tariff-rate quota (Minimum Access Volume) on the product
choices.B: A permanent ban on all imports of the product
choices.C: A reduction of the domestic industry's own production
choices.D: A requirement that exporters register with the Tariff Commission

316.reason: A definitive safeguard measure may take the form of a decrease in or imposition of a tariff-rate quota (Minimum Access Volume) on the product, among other forms (Primer p.94).

317.question: Under the special safeguard measure's volume test for SSG-denominated agricultural products, the additional duty should not exceed what fraction of the applicable out-quota customs duty?
317.reason: Under the volume test, the additional duty should not exceed one-third (1/3) of the applicable out-quota customs duty on the agricultural product (Primer p.95).

318.question: Under the special safeguard measure's price test, what additional duty applies if the price difference exceeds 10% but is at most 40% of the trigger price?

choices.B: Fifty percent (50%) of the amount exceeding the trigger price
choices.C: Thirty percent (30%) of the amount by which the price difference exceeds ten percent of the trigger price
choices.D: Ninety percent (90%) of the amount exceeding the trigger price

318.reason: Under the price test, if the price difference exceeds ten percent (10%) but is at most forty percent (40%) of the trigger price, the additional duty is thirty percent (30%) of the amount by which the price difference exceeds ten percent of the trigger price (Primer p.95).

319.question: What is the maximum initial period for the application of a definitive general safeguard measure, including the period the provisional measure was imposed?
319.reason: The maximum initial period for the application of a definitive general safeguard measure is four (4) years, including the period in which the provisional measure is imposed (Primer p.96).

320.question: To what maximum total period may a definitive general safeguard measure be extended?
320.reason: The initial period of a definitive general safeguard measure may be extended up to a maximum of ten (10) years (Primer p.96).

321.question: What is the maximum duration of a provisional general safeguard measure from the date of imposition?
321.reason: A provisional general safeguard measure shall not exceed 200 calendar days from the date of imposition (Primer p.95).

322.question: A special safeguard measure on SSG-denominated agricultural products remains in effect for how long?

choices.B: Only until the end of the year in which the measure is imposed
choices.C: Ten (10) years, same as general safeguard measures

322.reason: A special safeguard measure shall be in effect only until the end of the year in which the measure is imposed (Primer p.96).

323.question: When quantitative import restrictions are used as a general safeguard measure, such measures shall not reduce import quantity below what benchmark, absent clear justification?

choices.A: The average imports for the three (3) preceding representative years
choices.C: Fifty percent (50%) of current import levels
choices.D: The trigger volume used for special safeguards

323.reason: When quantitative import restrictions are used, such measures shall not reduce the quantity of imports below the average imports for the three (3) preceding representative years, unless clear justification is given (Primer p.96).

324.question: General safeguard measures shall not be applied to a product from a developing country if that country's share of total imports is less than what percentage, unless such countries collectively exceed nine percent?
324.reason: General safeguard measures shall not apply to a product from a developing country if its share of total imports is less than three percent (3%), provided developing countries with less than 3% share collectively account for not more than nine percent (9%) of total imports (Primer p.96).

325.question: Can the Tariff Commission recommend the application of general safeguard measures on a bilateral or selective basis against specific countries?

choices.A: Yes, provided the exporting country agrees in advance
choices.B: No, because safeguard measures must be applied on a non-selective or MFN basis irrespective of source
choices.C: Yes, but only against non-WTO member countries
choices.D: Yes, if the domestic industry specifically names the country in its petition

325.reason: One of the major guiding principles of the WTO Agreement on Safeguards is that measures be applied on a non-selective or MFN basis; a Member may not choose specific countries against whose exports it applies the measures (Primer p.96).

326.question: Does the Philippines generally have to pay compensation to affected WTO Members when it applies a general safeguard measure?

choices.A: No, safeguard measures never require compensation
choices.B: Yes, through compensation substantially equivalent to the level of concessions and obligations affected
choices.C: Only if the measure lasts more than ten years

326.reason: The Philippines, when applying safeguard measures, must generally pay compensation substantially equivalent to the level of concessions and other obligations affecting the exporting WTO Members (Primer p.97).

327.question: If no agreement on compensation is reached within how many days, may affected exporting WTO Members individually suspend substantially equivalent concessions (retaliate)?
327.reason: In the absence of an agreement on compensation within 30 days, the affected exporting Members may individually suspend substantially equivalent concessions, unless the Council for Trade in Goods disapproves (Primer p.97).

328.question: For how many years may the right to retaliate generally not be exercised, provided the safeguard measure resulted from an absolute increase in imports and conforms to the Safeguards Agreement?
328.reason: The right to retaliate may not be exercised for the first three (3) years that a safeguard measure is in effect, provided the measure resulted from an absolute increase in imports and conforms to the provisions of the Safeguards Agreement (Primer p.97).

329.question: An adjustment plan, as defined in the Primer, is best described as what?

choices.A: A government subsidy program for exporters
choices.B: The action plan of a domestic industry describing quantified goals, specific plans, and timetables to facilitate its positive adjustment to import competition

329.reason: An adjustment plan is the action plan of a domestic industry describing the set of quantified goals, specific plans, and timetables it commits to undertake to facilitate its positive adjustment to import competition (Primer p.97).

330.question: Within how many calendar days must the domestic industry submit its adjustment plan to the Tariff Commission, and how many days if the investigation is certified as urgent?

choices.B: 45 calendar days, or 30 calendar days if certified urgent

330.reason: The domestic industry submits its adjustment plan to the Tariff Commission within 45 calendar days, or 30 calendar days if the investigation is certified as urgent, upon receipt of the notice of submission (Primer p.97).

331.question: Does the Tariff Commission monitor an industry's implementation of its adjustment plan?

choices.A: No, monitoring is solely the responsibility of the Bureau of Customs
choices.B: Yes, including conduct of public hearings, on-site inspection, and data verification, with findings reported to the DA or DTI Secretary
choices.C: No, the plan is self-reported with no verification
choices.D: Yes, but only once at the end of the measure's duration

331.reason: The Commission monitors developments in the domestic industry's adjustment, including conduct of a public hearing and on-site inspection and data verification, and submits a report of findings and recommendations to the DA or DTI Secretary (Primer p.97).

332.question: According to the Table of Summary of Formal Investigations under Republic Act No. 8800, what was the final determination for the 2001 Cement case (Original Petition)?

choices.D: Measure not imposed for public interest

332.reason: The 2001 Cement case under RA No. 8800, filed as an Original Petition, had a Negative final determination (Primer p.98).

333.question: What was the outcome of the 2006 Sodium Tripolyphosphate - Technical Grade case under RA No. 8800?

choices.A: Positive, but the measure was not imposed for reason of public interest
choices.B: Negative, due to negligible import volume
choices.D: Positive, with the maximum duty imposed

333.reason: The 2006 Sodium Tripolyphosphate - Technical Grade case (Original Petition) resulted in a Positive determination, but the measure was not imposed for reason of public interest (Primer p.98).

334.question: In the 2006 Figured Glass, Clear and Tinted Float Glass and Glass Mirror case (First Extension), what happened to the measures on figured glass and glass mirror, respectively?

choices.A: Both were extended for another five years

343.question: According to the UNCTAD definition cited in the Primer, non-tariff measures (NTMs) are best described as what?

344.question: According to the Primer, how do Non-Tariff Barriers (NTBs) differ from Non-Tariff Measures (NTMs) in general?

choices.A: NTBs are a subset of NTMs applied with a protectionist or discriminatory intent or whose restrictiveness exceeds what is needed

choices.D: NTBs apply only to agricultural products while NTMs apply only to industrial goods

345.question: Which of the following is cited in the Primer as a reason why trade is regulated?

choices.D: To prevent any form of tariff collection

346.question: According to UNCTAD's classification cited in the Primer, NTMs are broadly classified into which two categories?

348.question: Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures (SPS), as described in the Primer's NTM classification, are measures aimed at what?

349.question: Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT), as a category of NTMs, relate to measures concerning what?

350.question: Pre-Shipment Inspection and Other Formalities, as a category of NTMs, comprise measures related to what?

351.question: Under the Primer's NTM classification, Contingent Trade-Protective Measures (Chapter D) include which of the following, more commonly known as trade remedy measures?
351.reason: Contingent Trade-Protective Measures include measures implemented to counteract the adverse effects of imports, including anti-dumping, countervailing, and safeguard measures, more commonly known as trade remedy measures (Primer p.104).

352.question: Price-control measures, as a category of NTMs, are implemented for which of the following purposes?

choices.B: To eliminate the need for an anti-dumping investigation
choices.C: To automatically grant duty exemptions to all importers
choices.D: To restrict the origin of a product's inputs only

352.reason: Price control measures are implemented to control or affect the prices of imported goods, such as to support the domestic price of certain products or to increase or preserve tax revenue (Primer p.105).

353.question: Finance measures, as an NTM category, restrict the payment of imports in what manner?

choices.A: By regulating the access and cost of foreign exchange, and imposing restrictions on terms of payment
choices.B: By banning all cash transactions for imported goods
choices.C: By requiring importers to use only domestic banks
choices.D: By eliminating letters of credit entirely

353.reason: Finance measures restrict the payment of imports, such as when the access and cost of foreign exchange is regulated, and also include restrictions on terms of payment (Primer p.105).

354.question: Which of the following is an example of a measure affecting competition, as described in the Primer's NTM classification?

355.question: Trade-related investment measures, as an NTM category, restrict investment in what way?

choices.D: By imposing a fixed foreign ownership ceiling of 40%

356.question: Restrictions on post-sales services, as an NTM category, refer to what kind of limitation imposed by importing countries?

choices.A: Restrictions on exporters' ability to provide post-sales services within the importing country's borders through preferred or desired channels

357.question: Under the Primer's NTM classification, subsidies are described as measures or practices by any level of government that involve what?

choices.D: A requirement that beneficiaries export all of their output

choices.B: The destination country of exported goods only

choices.D: A non-governmental organization with no formal international status

386.question: The GATT trade rounds developed rules for the Multilateral Trading System through how many rounds of negotiations, with which round being the most comprehensive and leading to the creation of the WTO?

choices.A: Six rounds, with the sixth (Tokyo Round) being the most comprehensive

389.question: Among the main objectives of the WTO listed in the Primer, which of the following is included?

choices.B: To eliminate all forms of international commerce
choices.C: To guarantee identical tariff rates for every WTO Member
choices.D: To centralize all customs administration under one global authority

389.reason: Among the main objectives of the WTO listed in the Agreement's preamble are to raise living standards and to ensure full employment (Primer p.120-121).

390.question: Which of the following is listed as a function of the WTO under Article III of the Agreement Establishing the WTO?

choices.B: To set binding domestic tax policy for all Members
choices.C: To directly manage the central banks of Member countries

390.reason: Among the main functions of the WTO is to serve as a forum for Members to settle their disputes (Primer p.121).

391.question: Which of the following is listed as a fundamental principle of the WTO?

choices.A: Non-discrimination, covering the Most-Favoured-Nation principle and the national treatment principle

392.question: Under the WTO's fundamental principles, what does the principle of special and differential treatment for less developed Members entail?

choices.D: Less developed Members are barred from participating in dispute settlement

393.question: According to the Primer, the highest decision-making body of the WTO, the Ministerial Conference, meets how often?

choices.D: Only when a trade dispute arises

394.question: The Ministerial Conference of the WTO is composed of what representatives from the Members?

choices.B: Only the Heads of State of each Member country

395.question: The General Council (GC), as the second level of the WTO's organizational structure, is composed of what kind of representatives?

choices.D: Only judges of the Dispute Settlement Body

396.question: When the General Council meets as the Dispute Settlement Body (DSB), what is its function?

choices.A: To establish panels of independent experts to resolve disputes, adopt rulings, and oversee their implementation
choices.B: To set tariff rates for Member countries
choices.D: To audit the financial statements of Member governments

397.question: The Trade Policy Review Body (TPRB), one of the forms the General Council takes, administers what?

choices.A: Trade policy reviews as mandated by the Trade Policy Review Mechanism of the WTO
choices.B: The negotiation of new free trade agreements
choices.C: The collection of countervailing duties across Members

398.question: At the third level of the WTO's organizational structure, the Councils and Subsidiary Bodies, which three councils report to the General Council?

choices.D: The Dispute Council, Accession Council, and Review Council

399.question: Which of the following is listed as a subsidiary body that reports directly to the WTO General Council on horizontal issues?

400.question: According to the Primer, how does the WTO generally make its decisions, following GATT's tradition?

choices.A: By majority vote of the Director-General alone

choices.C: By binding arbitration of a single appointed judge

684.reason: Negotiations came to a virtual halt in 2007 due to divergences on a number of core policy issues. (Primer p.224)

685.question: In which city does the WCO Technical Committee on Rules of Origin (WCO-TCRO) conduct its part of the Harmonization Work Programme?

686.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in the Primer as a goal of competition policy?

choices.A: Promote competitiveness in both domestic and foreign markets
choices.C: Maximize government revenue from import duties

686.reason: The Primer lists economic efficiency, correcting market failure, consumer welfare, higher economic growth and competitiveness in domestic and foreign markets as goals; maximizing import-duty revenue is not among them. (Primer p.226)

687.question: Among the five basic market structures described in the Primer, which one is similar to perfect competition but has many firms competing by producing similar but slightly different products?
687.reason: Monopolistic competition is described as similar to perfect competition, except that many firms compete by producing similar but slightly different products. (Primer p.226)

688.question: Which market structure is characterized by a small number of firms whose choices on strategic variables such as prices, product design, research and development, advertising and sales locations are strongly influenced by other firms in the industry?
688.reason: The Primer defines oligopoly as a market with a small number of firms where the quantity sold by any one firm is influenced by its strategic choices, which are strongly influenced by other firms. (Primer p.226)

689.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in the Primer as a source of market failure?
689.reason: The Primer lists public goods, income distribution, monopoly, externalities and information asymmetries as the sources of market failure; tariff escalation is not listed. (Primer p.227)

690.question: Under the Hilmer Report on National Competition Policy for Australia cited in the Primer, what are vertical agreements?

choices.A: Agreements by two manufacturers to fix the selling price of a product
choices.B: Agreements among competitors to share geographic markets
choices.C: Agreements among firms at the same level to bid jointly for a tender
choices.D: Collusion between firms at different stages of the production chain, such as suppliers and users of business inputs

690.reason: Vertical agreements involve firms at different stages of the production chain colluding, e.g., through quotas or exclusive dealings, while horizontal agreements are between enterprises at the same level of the market. (Primer p.227)

691.question: According to the Primer, what is the effect of using 'recommended prices' in relation to price-fixing agreements among competitors?

choices.A: They are less obvious than direct price-fixing but in reality involve the fixing of prices by agreement
choices.B: They are always lawful because the prices are only suggestions
choices.C: They are treated as retail price maintenance only
choices.D: They are allowed only for goods covered by the Price Act

691.reason: The Primer states that the use of recommended prices is less obvious than outright price-fixing but in reality involves the fixing of prices by agreement. (Primer p.228)

692.question: Which anti-competitive conduct is an agreement between competitors to limit dealings with a particular supplier or customer, such as a boycott, to prevent new firms from entering the market or to force existing firms out?
692.reason: An exclusionary provision limits dealings with a particular supplier, customer or class of customer (e.g., boycotts) to keep new firms out or push existing firms out of the market. (Primer p.228)

693.question: Which anti-competitive conduct refers to action by suppliers, manufacturers or wholesalers specifying a minimum price below which goods or services may not be resold or advertised for resale?
693.reason: Retail price maintenance is the specification of a minimum price below which goods or services may not be resold or advertised for resale. (Primer p.228)

694.question: Applying dissimilar pricing or conditions to equivalent transactions is an example of which type of anti-competitive behavior described in the Primer?

choices.D: Limiting production, markets or technical development

694.reason: The Primer gives applying dissimilar pricing or conditions to equivalent transactions and vice-versa as the example of discriminatory behavior. (Primer p.229)

695.question: Which solution to anti-competitive conduct is described as the most direct form of anti-competitive measure that an authority can undertake, applying to activities detrimental to regular competitive behavior such as price fixing?
695.reason: Per se prohibition is the most direct measure, applying to activities detrimental to regular competitive behavior in a market, e.g., price fixing. (Primer p.229)

696.question: Which mechanism allows the public benefits from ostensibly anti-competitive conduct to be assessed as a counter-balancing consideration, and includes direct intervention or inquiry by a government commission?
696.reason: Authorization is the mechanism through which public benefits from ostensibly anti-competitive conduct are weighed as a counter-balancing consideration. (Primer p.229)

697.question: What is the distinguishing feature of a natural monopoly according to the Primer?

choices.A: A single firm holds exclusive government-granted rights to the product
choices.B: Two or more firms jointly set the market price
choices.C: A single facility can supply the entire market demand more efficiently than two or more smaller facilities
choices.D: Entry is blocked by a ban on foreign investment

697.reason: The Primer states that a single facility being able to supply the entire market demand more efficiently than two or more smaller facilities is the distinguishing feature of a natural monopoly. (Primer p.230)

698.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in the Primer as a source of barriers to entry that results from regulation affecting competition?

choices.A: Economies of scale due to market share achieved by incumbents
choices.B: Subsidies granted to new entrants by the Tariff Commission
choices.D: Capital requirements, including investment in brand development through advertising

698.reason: The listed sources are economies of scale, capital requirements, cost savings from incumbents' experience, monopoly access to key infrastructure and monopoly of key industry knowledge; subsidies to new entrants are not listed. (Primer p.230)

699.question: Within the framework of competition policy, an essential facility is a major infrastructure exhibiting which two characteristics?

choices.A: It is essential to the effective operation of an economic organization and exhibits natural monopoly characteristics
choices.B: It is government-owned and exempt from competition law
choices.C: It is located within an economic zone and serves only exporters
choices.D: It is privately financed and open to all competitors free of charge

699.reason: An essential facility is essential to the effective operation of an economic organization and has natural monopoly characteristics, e.g., electricity grids, rail infrastructure, roads, port facilities, pipelines and telecommunications networks. (Primer p.230)

700.question: According to the Primer, competition policy and law need to ensure that workable competition is maintained in which type of industries?
700.reason: One of the main concerns listed is ensuring that workable competition is maintained in oligopolistic industries. (Primer p.231)

701.question: Competition policy and law need to monitor mergers between independent enterprises because the merger may result in what?

choices.A: Higher tariff revenue and lower imports
choices.B: Market concentration and reduction in competition
choices.C: Greater price transparency in the industry

701.reason: The Primer lists monitoring of mergers where the effect may be market concentration and a reduction in competition as a main concern. (Primer p.231)

702.question: Which formal body was established by the ASEAN Economic Ministers (AEM) in August 2007 to discuss and coordinate competition policies of ASEAN Member States?
702.reason: The AEGC is a formal body established by the AEM in August 2007 to act as a regional forum on competition policies. (Primer p.232)

703.question: The ASEAN Experts Group on Competition (AEGC) is composed of representatives from the competition authorities of all ASEAN Member States nominated by whom?

704.question: Which strategic measure of the ASEAN Competition Action Plan 2016-2025 involves establishing platforms for regular exchange and engagement, encouraging competition compliance and creating an enhanced regional web portal for competition policy and law?

choices.A: Establish effective competition regimes by putting in place competition laws for AMSs that do not have them

705.question: Which strategic measure of the ASEAN Competition Action Plan 2016-2025 calls for developing a regional strategy on convergence?

707.question: According to Table 9.1 of the Primer, which is the competition authority of Thailand?

713.question: On what date of every year does Proclamation No. 384 (s. 2012) declare National Competition Day?

714.question: Among the powers of the Philippine Competition Commission (PCC) listed in the Primer, a subpoena duces tecum is issued to require what?

719.question: Which international organization, in 1998, defined e-commerce as the production, distribution, marketing, sale or delivery of goods and services by electronic means?

choices.C: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD)

724.question: Which author's 2017 description defines digital trade as commerce involving more than one country for which the product itself is digital and/or advertising, ordering, delivering, payment or servicing is accomplished at least in part using the internet or similar digital technology?

736.question: Which law is described in the Primer as the primary law on e-commerce in the Philippines?

741.question: Which of the following is NOT among the recommendations of Serafica and Albert (2018) for the Philippines to take advantage of digital trade?
